changes.implementation_notes: Prereg doc only.

changes.name: Leg unit unchanged: ATR-risk sizing (one power of sigma) is Kelly-correct because avgR is flat across vol terciles, and margin per unit of ATR risk is leverage-invariant under PM
changes.rule: shares = risk_bps x NAV / (stop_atr x ATR), Wilder/simple ATR as today; no sigma^alpha change; no ATR% / 200-SMA / tier / VIX / P-C / current-dial tiers inside any strategy.
changes.math: Within-strategy vol terciles 2010+: avgR 0.455 / 0.433 / 0.519 (N ~1,265 each); OVS +0.33 / +0.41 / +0.40 (t 0.99), OLV non-monotone, 52wh +0.70 / +0.41 / +0.48. Margin per $ ATR risk = rate / (k x ATR%): single stock 15% / (1.25 x 2.5%) = 4.8; 3x ETF under PM 45% / (1.25 x 7.5%) = 4.8; under rules-based 90% short = 9.6; sub-$17 stock short at $5/sh on a $10 stock = 16. Ledger: 52wh 3.3, OLV 4.4, index dip-buys 5.3-5.4 (TIMS) vs 10 at flat 15%, OVS 6.3, 3x fades 9.1-9.3 (18 rules), Sector BO 10.0, WCDS 10.5; book 6.33.
changes.expected_effect: None; codifies that the GRM step and the L1 tilt are spent in risk units, and that the only legs deserving a margin haircut per unit of risk are 3x shorts under rules-based margin and cheap-stock shorts.
changes.confidence: high
changes.evidence: baseline plan L0; signal_quality finding 8 (594 tests, nothing passes on ATR%, 200-SMA, tier, VIX, P/C, current dial); growthmax_1 margin_per_risk_by_strategy; broker base rates (TIMS leverage-scaled stress).
changes.risks: None.
changes.intuition: One ATR of risk buys the same R in a quiet name as a wild one; the unit is right, and under portfolio margin it costs the same margin whether the instrument is 1x or 3x.
changes.implementation_notes: None.

changes.name: No calendar-conditional sizing layer; flow state is the only 'seasonal' variable that sizes; the dip-buy May-Oct cell is a watch item with a written trigger
changes.rule: No multiplier may reference month, quarter, half-year, earnings season, opex week, turn-of-month, day-of-week or holiday adjacency (decision register: closed negative). The L4 drawdown/growth frontier is computed on the full-year series and never re-derived per season; no vol-target may key on seasonally low realised vol. Earnings handling stays per name (OVS blackout, OLV/St OS overrides per GM-21). Watch item: if the dip-buy family's expanding May-Oct minus Nov-Apr gap stays below -0.15 AND the September dip-buy cell (R/risk 0.03, N 70) is <= 0 after 20 more September fills (~2029), re-open a 0.75x Sep-only appetite decision. Cycle: keep OVS cycle_risk_mults {2: 0.75} only.
changes.math: 1,012 strategy-by-calendar cells: zero BH-FDR 10% survivors on year-paired tests (min q 0.27), zero Bonferroni; fitted strat x month multipliers WF +0.04 Sharpe (t 1.0) and LOYO -0.056 with maxDD 2.6 pts worse; every other dimension <= baseline in both designs. Daily variance is seasonal (May-Oct sd 63 vs 83 bps, t -3.19) but so is the mean (7.1 vs 11.6 bps) because both are open risk (Spearman sd vs open risk 0.77): Kelly ratio May-Oct / Nov-Apr 1.06 pooled, 1.03 median. Prior replays: Sep 0.5x -4.5% P&L (1/24 years), May-Oct 0.75x -11.3% (maxDD unchanged), Nov-Apr 1.25x Sharpe -0.033 / maxDD -3.0, Dec 1.25x +0.003, single-stock earnings-season 0.75x -7.1% (0-1 of 17-24 years). In-season trades are BETTER after the blackouts (0.56 vs 0.43 book, 14/15 strategies same sign, LOYO +0.06..+0.22).
changes.expected_effect: Zero P&L change vs today; avoids -1% to -11% P&L and 0 to -2.6 pt maxDD from every replayed calendar rule; midterm book cut rejected (Sharpe 2.515 -> 2.521, risk-matched maxDD 0.5 pt worse).
changes.confidence: high
changes.evidence: seasonality_flow findings 1-9 and recommendations 1-6; cycle_macro finding 3 and recommendation 1; outside calendar pack (TOM decayed to insignificance in US large-cap post-2015 and re-anchored by T+1 settlement; opex +0.2%/week and fading; Halloween insignificant on the S&P since 1984; September t ~ -1 vs zero; January effect untradeable; pre-holiday gone; pre-FOMC drift gone post-2015).
changes.risks: Small strategies (3x fades, St OS Sznl, Sector BO, MWC) have 1-14 trades per month cell; absence of evidence there is a power statement.
changes.intuition: The book's trades are conditional entries with ATR exits; an index month base rate does not describe the conditional cell, and where flow is high the marginal signal is average, not poor.
changes.implementation_notes: Decision-register entry plus negative-registry list (below).

seasonality_rules: S-1 No calendar multiplier of any kind: 0 of 1,012 strategy x calendar cells survive FDR on year-clustered tests; every fitted calendar table is at or below baseline out of sample in 17 of 18 rule/design combinations; unfitted priors replay negative (Sep 0.5x -4.5% P&L 1/24 yrs; Aug-Sep 0.75x -3.9%; May-Oct 0.75x -11.3% with maxDD unchanged; Nov-Apr 1.25x Sharpe -0.033 maxDD -3.0; Dec/Q4 1.25x +0.003/-0.022; opex dip-buy 0.75x -1.2%; TOM 0.75x -7.0%; OLV Aug 0.5x -0.9%; LT Trend Jun 0.5x +0.3%; 52wh Oct 1.5x -0.001).

S-2 Seasonal variance is flow, not risk: May-Oct book sd 63 vs 83 bps/day (t -3.19, lower in 19/24 summers) with mean 7.1 vs 11.6 bps; Kelly ratio 1.06 pooled / 1.03 median; sd tracks open risk (Spearman 0.77, elasticity 0.51). The GRM frontier (GM-1) is computed on the whole-year bootstrap and never per season; no vol-target may key on seasonally low realised vol (the summer 'low vol, add leverage' mistake) and no season may cut size (the winter 'high vol, cut' mistake).

S-3 Signal FLOW is the only time-varying state that sizes, and it sizes UP: family trailing-5d candidate count top tercile -> 1.25x base (GM-14) and cap x1.5 (GM-13); same-day breadth and OVS own-count >= 5 are second-stage prereg refinements (GM-22). No down-size on low flow; no 'crowded selloff' cut in any mean-reverting family (top tercile earns 1.7-2.7x the P&L per unit risk of the bottom tercile). Breakout family gets no flow rule.

S-4 Earnings handling stays per name, never per season: keep the OVS +/-10 TD blackout and the St OS Sznl -5..-1 override; restore OLV's pre-print size (GM-21); reject any 'trim single stocks in reporting season' rule (in-season trades run avgR 0.52-0.64 vs 0.41-0.48 off-season, 14/15 strategies same sign, LOYO +0.06..+0.22; single-stock 0.75x in season costs -7.1% P&L, 0-1 of 17-24 years better).

S-5 Dip-buy family May-Oct: full size; WATCH ITEM only. Family May-Oct avgR 0.301 vs Nov-Apr 0.494 (t_ep -2.12, LOYO [-0.25,-0.14], 6/6 members, post-2013 only, control opposite-signed). Trigger: expanding gap < -0.15 AND September dip-buy R/risk (0.03, N 70) <= 0 after +20 September fills (~2029) -> re-open a 0.75x Sep-only appetite decision. At 7-15% of Kelly a +0.30 R/risk cell keeps full size; the gated walk-forward cut lost in each of the 4 years it fired.

S-6 Presidential cycle: keep OVS cycle_risk_mults {2: 0.75} (6/6 midterm years below, year-clustered t -2.00); no midterm cut for the rest of the book (ex-OVS year t -1.33; 0.75x book cut Sharpe-neutral with risk-matched maxDD 0.5 pt worse; the book's worst drawdowns are 2008/2020 election and 2015 pre-election years). Re-exam trigger: a midterm year whose OVS P1 avgR exceeds the other-year mean 0.37.

S-7 January excess variance is episodic (8 of 24 Januaries above 1.3x, median ratio 0.99) and January per-trade quality is average (0.49R, N 350): no January de-rate; the January tail is the L3 hedge's territory (dial episodes 2008/2015/2016/2021/2022 all had high open risk into a selloff). December's lower trade-R variance is OVS composition: no December up-size.

S-8 Friday MTM weakness (3.6 vs 10.3 bps/day, 21/24 years) is a holding-day effect, half structural (MonFri/Monday Dip flat on Fridays): nothing for sizing, which keys on the signal date; at most a hedge-timing or exit-day question outside scope.

S-9 Outside calendar priors that do transfer as tie-breakers only, never as multipliers: month-end selling pressure T-8..T-4 then reversal (Etula, re-anchored to T-1 since T+1 settlement 2024-05-28, unconfirmed in repo); opex-week small long tilt; Monday-weak/Friday-strong in speculative names (Birru); January weak for 52-week-high momentum (George-Hwang, Sias); momentum-crash regimes after >15-20% declines with high vol (Daniel-Moskowitz) support NOT frag-banding the 3x leader/bear fades and NOT vol-boosting breakouts there. Any in-repo seasonal cell that ever passes must be sized at 0.5-0.75x its in-sample edge and capped at +/-25% of base bps (McLean-Pontiff decay).

S-10 Retired from any future study list (negative registry): September 0.5x, Aug-Sep 0.75x, May-Oct 0.75x book, Nov-Apr 1.25x book, December 1.25x, Q4 1.25x, opex-week dip-buy cut, turn-of-month tilts, holiday-adjacent tilts, OLV August cut, LT Trend June cut, 52wh October boost, OVS December boost, January de-rate, Friday de-rate, single-stock earnings-season haircut, book midterm cut, calendar-month hedge threshold.
what_not_to_do: Do not add any book-level scalar: no vol target (EWMA cut-only 2.70 / two-sided 2.54 vs baseline 2.81 at equal vol), no VIX inverse (2.63), no dial step or taper (2.81-2.82), no open-leg 1/sqrt(n) (2.74), no dial-conditioned pooled or per-strategy caps (PIT t -0.23, taper -11.4R), no vol-state family scalar (MR family 0.75x at rv21 < 12: +0.02-0.05 Sharpe in sample, negative 2016+). Cederburg 2020 and DeMiguel 2024: real-time vol management lowers OOS Sharpe for the market/beta leg and most non-momentum anomalies.

Do not add drawdown-triggered de-risking of any form (Grossman-Zhou continuous, Millennium 5%/7.5% step cuts, trailing-P&L throttles): the book's daily P&L autocorrelation is NEGATIVE (lags 1-2, 5 at -0.03 to -0.06; sum lags 1-5 -0.12 to -0.13, se 0.013-0.019) and forward 21d returns are HIGHER inside drawdowns (dd 5-10%: +22% / +55% ann vs +22% / +34% outside); Kaminski-Lo 2014: the stopping premium is negative under mean-reverting P&L; Man 2025: a 20% cut-off rule cost 2.2%/yr on uncorrelated Sharpe-0.5 strategies.

Do not size DOWN on high signal flow in any mean-reverting family (the 'crowded selloff' hypothesis is wrong-signed: dip_buy PnL/risk 0.572 top vs 0.212 bottom tercile; oversold_hold 0.835 vs 0.314; short_fade 0.687 vs 0.331); do not generalise the 3x Bear same-day derate to OVS; do not use 0.5x/1.5x flow multipliers (worse than 0.75/1.25 on Sharpe in every family); do not add a breakout flow rule (17 variables, 3 forms, all at or below baseline).

Do not add correlation-, sector-, same-ticker- or stack-age-keyed cuts inside any strategy, no Kelly-concurrency 1/(1 + n rho) or variance-parity per-leg rule, no OLV sleeve open-risk cap (-$70k/16y for -$3.4k worst-21d), no sqrt-n marginal budget (0.64 vs 0.79 PnL/risk): every one cuts the higher-edge leg (rho > 0.6 cuts lose 0.02-0.04 PnL/risk in OLV, OVS, WCDS, LT, 3x ETF; same-ticker 0.5x on OLV 0.715 vs 0.790). Ex-ante 63d correlation with the open names carries no information about a leg's R (Spearman -0.04 to +0.16).

Do not arm a hedge, a cut or any beta control on VIX level (-$158.5k, 0 of 15 episodes positive, t -3.85), VIX percentile (-$154k), SPY or book drawdown state (-$139k), or run an always-on hedge (-$478k, maxDD -8.3% -> -11.5%); do not use QQQ (lowest R2 in every regime) or IWM (its extra P&L is the small-cap factor's -31.9% armed-day drift, not fit) as the instrument; do not run hedge ratios above 1.0x of beta_hat or 42d/63d betas (zero predictive correlation with realised beta when armed); do not arm at 65/60 as the primary (PIT t 0.99, a Feb-2020 result); do not hedge the dip-buy family + OLV only (one third to two thirds of the whole-book hedge). Do not use realised vol as a stand-in for the dial anywhere: the book's beta is HIGHEST in low-VIX near-the-highs tape and LOWEST after vol arrives (VIX 30+: beta 0.17, Sharpe 3.8).

Do not tier any strategy on the current-weights dial series or re-open 0.5x-at-65 exemption cuts for OLV or OVS: the OLV dial gradient (t -3.24, LOYO 80%) is a recompute-vintage artefact that vanishes on the PIT dial on the same 211 trades (t +0.03); the book's PIT [65,999) cell is +0.006R (t 0.04), OLV's +0.235R, OVS P1's -0.104R (t -0.84). Do not cite the retired 2026-08-24 OLV band as evidence (it was an explicit appetite decision, reversed the next session). Do not add within-strategy tiers on VIX, P/C fear percentile, ATR%, 200-SMA distance, universe tier, days-since-last-signal, sector breadth or the WCDS move size (594 tests; the passers sit inside the ~27-hit false-positive budget).
Do not add any calendar multiplier (month, quarter, half, earnings season, opex, TOM, day-of-week, holiday, midterm-book) or a seasonal vol target; see S-1..S-10 and the retired list.

Do not remove the per-strategy 250 bps cap on high-flow days (x99 on short_fade: Sharpe 1.18 -> 0.93, maxDD -$44k -> -$127k) or fragility-condition either cap; do not double OVS P2 sizing everywhere (0.280 vs 0.298 PnL/risk): the P2 edge lives in extremity (GM-9) and its aggregate cap (GM-10), not in base P2 bps.

Do not rebuild any P(win)-based selectivity layer (ML meta-labelling deleted 2026-08-07: win rate and expectancy are decoupled in this book; the bucket it wanted to SKIP averaged +0.60R). Every quality claim in this plan is expectancy-based (avgR, R per unit risk, mu/sigma^2); GM-9's OVS cut is the one cell where both move together.

Do not switch the sizing base to live NAV today (a 16% risk cut, since NLV $632k < $750k) and do not full-compound before the live-vs-ledger haircut is measured under 25%; do not rebase downward after a drawdown (ratchet only, GM-4).

Do not spend any of the GRM step on the overflow-tier LONG strategies (survivorship keep 0.85, overflow avgR <= liquid in every shared strategy, 2x the impact, ADV participation already 1-2.7% p90 in three of them) and do not raise the two pilots (3x Leader Gap Fade N 24, Monthly Weak Close N 14) on their own point estimates (0.5x mean prior until N >= 50; MWC's per-trade Sharpe 3.5 at N 14 is not a number to size to).

Do not add a hard NOTIONAL cap as a risk control (McKinley's standing rule; the retired 100%-NAV OLV book cap stays retired; the 25%-NAV no-stop-short cap stays rejected). The margin-feasibility guard (GM-2) is a broker-constraint control and is the single exception, framed as such; if that framing is not accepted, GRM stays at 2.25 and the step to 3.0 is off.

Do not trust the GBM drawdown formulas (x^(2/c-1)) or the block bootstrap for jump risk at GRM >= 3: Thorp's 1987 warning (2x leverage -> 2.85x before rebalance) applies to the OLV no-stop stacks and gap-through shorts; the per-strategy cap, the OLV ticker cap, the gap-through stop-fill model and the margin guard are the jump-risk controls, and the GRM rule's max-day term is what keeps a 1987-style day survivable.

Do not extend the 3x Bear same-day derate, add stacking rules to the 3x fades, or move the 52wh open-leg threshold back to >= 5 (the exact-5 cell is 1.71R on 13 legs); do not extend gap_size_derate to IOB or Monthly Weak Close (opposite sign).
narrative:
Where the book sits. On its own flat-basis daily series the book has a Sharpe of 1.97 (2003+) or 2.67 (2016+) at 11.5-12.5% annualised vol. After the measured 40% haircut on the mean (keep 0.60, range 0.29-0.73, from selection deflation x 2026 realisation x survivorship x costs) the haircut Sharpe is 1.2-1.6 and the full-Kelly multiple of current sizing is 10.3-12.8x. Current sizing is therefore 8-10% of haircut Kelly and 5-7% of raw Kelly; exact E[log(1+m r)] is linear in m to within one point through m = 3 on every window and every haircut (at 40%: 12.9 / 18.8 / 24.5 / 34.8% per year at m 1 / 1.5 / 2 / 3 on 2003+, 19.3 / 28.4 / 37.0 / 53.3% on 2016+). Growth theory has nothing to say against any size the account can carry, and the principal has removed the drawdown constraint. So the plan is decided by two boundaries and one allocation question.

Boundary one is portfolio margin, and it moved when the rates were tiered. The unconstrained study charged every non-3x leg 15% and found the 2016-06-14 broad-index dip-buy cluster (418% gross, all long) as the wall at m 1.60. Under TIMS (broad index 8%, small-cap index 10%, single and sector 15%, 3x 45%, cheap-short per-share floors) that day needs 48% of NAV and the binding day becomes 2023-02-03, a 3x-ETF-fade short cluster with 54% of a 180% gross in leveraged ETFs: 56% of NAV at current size, so m_max = 1.79 on the $750k base and 1.51 on the live $632k NLV, with the p99 day binding only at m 2.39 on live NLV. Two things follow. GRM 2.25 (m 1.5) is feasible today with the max day exactly at live NLV, and a step to 3.0 is a p99-day question that the order_staging margin guard settles (requirement > 70% of NLV on 0.5 days/yr at m 1.5, 2.6 at m 2). And the decisive unknown is not the broad-index cluster any more but whether IBKR charges 3x ETFs at 45% or at the rules-based 75/90%: under the latter the CURRENT book already needs 99% of NAV on 2023-02-03, which is why GM-3's what-if calibration of that specific book precedes the step. Boundary two is the per-strategy 250 bps cap, which saturates the realised multiple near 4.6x and costs one point of growth at m 1.5 and three at m 2; it stays fixed because it alone bounds the worst single day, except where the within-strategy and flow analyses show the cap-bound days are the best days (OVS to 375; x1.5 relief on family top-tercile flow days), which together add ~4-8% of book P&L with Sharpe up and tails byte-identical. Liquidity is nowhere near binding (edge halves at m ~58; overflow ATR Extended Gap Up at m ~12), which is why the GRM step is routed to the liquid tier, index legs and the short book while overflow longs hold their effective bps (GM-6).

The allocation question is answered by keep-weighted Kelly. Replacing the plan's flat 50% mu shrinkage with each strategy's measured keep and clipping the Sigma^-1 mu weights to [0.5, 1.6] walks forward at 29.3% a year against 24.2% equal and 28.0% for the plan's half-blend, Sharpe 2.16 vs 2.05 / 2.14, 10 of 13 years better, worst held-out year -7.9% (the half-blend's is -12.5%), cumulative +68 points of NAV vs +51, at a maxDD of -14.7% vs -12.1% that this lens accepts. The tilt cuts the four strategies that own 61% of worst-5%-day losses for 36% of P&L (52wh, Sector BO, WCDS, IOB, plus St OS Sznl) and raises the diversifiers (MonFri, OLV, LT Trend, ATR Ext, the 3x fades), and because the cut strategies are the margin-heavy ones (WCDS 10.5 and Sector BO 10.0 margin dollars per risk dollar vs OLV 4.4 and the index dip-buys 5.3) the tilted book uses 35% less mean margin than equal weights: the tilt funds most of the GRM step. The 3x ETF Fade's raise is capped at 1.25 rather than 1.60 because it owns the binding margin day. OVS is held at 1.0 on base bps and gets its growth through the two caps and the extremity redeployment (0.5x below mean rank 94, 1.25x above, +12.9% R per unit risk at constant risk, 17/24 years).

Within strategies every rule sizes by marginal expected R, never by marginal sleeve variance, because at 8-15% of Kelly the variance tax on a marginal leg is second order and the Euler lens loses at equal risk in every strategy where correlation is high. OLV's ladder is re-keyed to max(ticker recency, sleeve depth) with a 1.25x rung at six or more open (P&L $418k -> $584k, PnL/risk 0.790 -> 0.839, better exit-basis tails), WCDS and LT Trend run solo 0.75 / adds 1.25 (both improve P&L per risk and maxDD together), OLV gets a 1.25x pullback tilt when SPY is 3-10% off its high (11/15 walk-forward years, book Sharpe +0.02-0.04, maxDD unchanged), and the clone controls are kept as variance-only rules (IOB SPY+QQQ 0.5x, dip-buy same-ticker clamps, 52wh 0.5x at six-plus open instead of five). Flow is the one state variable that sizes, and it sizes up: 1.25x base and cap x1.5 on family top-tercile candidate-count days (17/17 years, +9.9% P&L, Sharpe 2.20 -> 2.22), with the dip-buy leg gated to dial < 50 where the flow edge is absent.

Cross-strategy, the dial moves correlation and beta, not variance or edge: effective N falls 4.4 -> 3.1 and the SPY-explained share of book variance triples (10% -> 31%) between calm tape and dial 65+, while the book's beta is highest in low-VIX near-the-highs tape and lowest after vol arrives. The math says hedge the embedded beta when its conditional drift turns negative and never cut the idiosyncratic book: the dial-armed whole-book ES hedge at 50/45 with a 126d beta passes its pre-registered ship rule on point-in-time weights (+$104k, 10/13 episodes, t 1.68, Sharpe 2.90 -> 3.04, bootstrap P 0.046, placebo rank 1.000) and every VIX- or drawdown-armed alternative loses in nearly all episodes. LT Trend ST OS is the one exemption that fails PIT at the 50 line and gets a plain 0.5x band; OLV and OVS stay exempt with PIT support, and the plan's current-weights '65+ halves' table is withdrawn.

What the plan refuses, with numbers, is as load-bearing as what it adds: no book scalar (nine overlays at or below baseline at equal vol), no drawdown cut (daily ACF -0.03 to -0.06, forward returns higher inside drawdowns, Kaminski-Lo), no calendar layer (0 of 1,012 cells), no down-size on flow, no correlation cuts, no VIX-armed hedge, no dial tiers on the recompute vintage, no notional caps as risk controls, no P(win) selectivity, no compounding before the live haircut is measured, and no GRM spent on the overflow-long tier or the pilots. The drawdown this accepts at GRM 2.25 with the tilt is a 1-year median of ~11-12% and p95 of ~20-23%, P(1y DD > 20%) 2-5%, P(3y DD > 30%) 0-2%, a ~20% maxDD and ~-10% worst day on the actual 2003-2026 path, and at GRM 3.0 roughly 1.35x those figures with P(3y DD > 30%) 3-10%; under GBM the lifetime odds of ever seeing a 20% drawdown are 3-6% at 2.25 and 7-13% at 3.0. Every number is on the flat $750k ledger basis with the vintages stated in the evidence pack; the growth-side numbers stay in-sample until the broker-fill reconciliation (GM-7) replaces the 40% haircut with a measured one, and the boundary-side numbers stay stylised until the IBKR what-if (GM-3) replaces the assumed rates.

lens: risk-architect: tails, correlation dynamics, hedging, margin, capacity, sequencing risk of compounding. Sizes themes not tickers, hedges what the dial detects, and puts every stack and clone on a risk budget that is a tail formula, not a variance tax.
thesis: The book is a six-theme portfolio running at 7-8% of its haircut Kelly with pairwise theme correlation 0.06 and an effective N of 4.4-4.7 themes; its tail is not a correlation event (average theme correlation on the worst 5% of days is -0.13, effective N 17) but a composition event, one theme fully loaded on its own worst day. Growth is linear in size through GRM 3 and drawdown appetite is not the binding constraint; the two real walls are the portfolio-margin requirement on the handful of long-cluster days that are also the book's best days (plain PM feasibility m 1.6-1.8 on the max day, ~1.0-1.15 under concentration or rules-based 3x rates, tighter on the live $632k NLV) and single-day gap loss on no-stop stacks (book stress multiple k = realized day loss / open ATR risk: p99 0.91, p99.9 1.28, max 1.86). So: raise GRM to 2.25 in two steps behind a margin-feasibility guard and the dial-armed whole-book beta hedge; keep the flat $750k base with a downside rebase floor and half-compounding above it; allocate risk by theme variance budget (cut breakout, raise dip-buy-index and oversold-hold) with per-strategy keep factors as the mu shrinkage; size adds by marginal expected R and bound stacks only by a theme one-day loss formula that binds past the p99; hedge the factor the dial detects instead of cutting the idiosyncratic book; and add no calendar, vol-target, drawdown-cut or correlation-spike layer anywhere, because every one of them is a closed negative result here and outside.

grm.value: 2.25 (m = 1.5x current sizing), reached in two steps: GRM 2.0 (m 1.33) immediately; GRM 2.25 once (a) the margin-feasibility guard in order_staging is live, (b) the P1 dial-armed hedge has logged one paper episode, and (c) IBKR what-if margin has been queried on the 2016-06-14, 2019-06-26, 2023-02-03 and 2025-01-10 books scaled by m. GRM 2.5-3.0 is reachable only after the index legs of the dip-buy family move to ES/MES/NQ/MNQ (lifts the plain-PM wall from m ~1.6-1.8 to ~2.3-3.0) and the measured live-vs-ledger haircut comes in at or under 40%. The per-strategy 250 bps daily cap stays FIXED in effective bps through 2.25 (cost ~1 pt of growth; it bounds the one day that was the entire uncapped maxDD).
grm.rationale: Growth math: g(m) = E[log(1 + m r)] is linear to within 1 pt through m = 3 on every window and haircut (risk_arch_04 / unconstrained_growth). At the measured 40% haircut on the daily mean (estimation_haircut central; range 27-71%) the book at GRM 1.5 is 7.7% of Kelly (2016-07+, Sharpe_h 1.66, vol 12.9%); m 1.5 takes it to 11.6% of Kelly (growth share 22%), m 2.0 to 15.5% (29%). Ann. log growth at h = 0.40: 2016-07+ 21.9% (m 1) -> 25.6% (1.25) -> 30.4% (1.5) -> 35.1% (1.75) -> 39.7% (2.0); 2003+ 13.4% -> 16.5% -> 19.5% -> 22.5% -> 25.4%. At the pessimistic 71% haircut the 2003+ growth is still positive (6.1% -> 8.7% at m 1.5) but the historical-path maxDD replay goes to -63.5%, which is the reading that says the haircut, not the drawdown, is what the GRM depends on. Outside base rates (Thorp/Benter/Ziemba 1/4-1/2 of honest Kelly; Carver half-Sharpe-then-half-Kelly ~25% of backtest Kelly; Busseti-Ryu-Boyd risk-constrained Kelly tolerating P 10% of a 30% drawdown) all sit ABOVE m 1.5, so nothing in the sizing literature argues against the step and the 2026-07 GRM replay found no cliff (Sharpe 1.89/1.87/1.85/1.83 across 1.0-1.75). What stops the number at 2.25 is not drawdown but two step functions: (1) margin: on my class map (stock 15% / index 8% / 3x 45%) the historical max-requirement day (2023-02-03) needs 55% of the base at m 1 -> feasible m 1.81 on $750k, 1.52 on the live $632k NLV; the finer-class growth study gets 1.60 / 1.34; with a 30% concentration rate on stocks the max day needs 87% (m 1.15); rules-based 90% on short 3x legs makes 2023-02-03 need 99% (m 1.01). The p99 requirement day is 35% -> m 2.9 on the base, 2.4 on live NLV. Those max days are long dip-buy clusters that carry 49% of the book's PnL, so the answer is to guard them (GM-4) and re-instrument them (GM-5), not to shrink the book to fit them. (2) Live NLV: the flat $750k base on a $632k account already runs 1.19x its intended fraction; GRM 2.25 is 1.78x in NAV terms, which lands exactly on the plain-PM max-day wall on live NLV (1.81 x 0.843 = 1.52 ~ m 1.5). Hence the two-step path: 2.0 now is inside every wall on the p99 day and inside the max-day wall on the base; 2.25 needs the guard.
grm.drawdown_accepted: At GRM 2.25 with the 40% haircut, unhedged, block bootstrap (mean block 10, 2000 x 1y / 1500 x 3y paths): 2016-07+: 1y median maxDD 9.9%, p95 17.3%, P(1y DD > 15%) 11%, P(1y DD > 20%) 2%; 3y median 13.1%, P(3y DD > 20%) 8%, P(3y DD > 30%) 1%; historical-path replay maxDD -15.9% (-14.3% with the P1 hedge), worst day -7.4%. 2003+: 1y median 10.7%, p95 19.9%, P(>15%) 20%, P(>20%) 5%; 3y median 15.5%, P(>20%) 21%, P(>30%) 2%; historical path -24.7%, worst day -8.9%. At GRM 2.0 (m 1.33, interpolated): 1y median ~9%, P(1y > 20%) ~1-3%, historical path -14 to -22%. At the 71% haircut edge of the range, GRM 2.25 gives P(1y DD > 20%) 12-13% and a 2003+ historical-path DD of -63.5%: that is the cost of being wrong about the edge, not about the size, and it is why the haircut is re-measured before any step past 2.25. Continuous-time cross-check (GBM, fraction c of haircut Kelly at m 1.5 = 0.116): P(ever DD >= 20%) 2.7%, >= 30% 0.3%; the bootstrap is fatter than lognormal, as it should be. Time to recover from the trough of a year's max DD: median 14-30 sessions, p95 61-112 (unconstrained_growth). Single-day: with book open ATR risk p99 544 bps (max 773) and stress multiple k_99.9 = 1.28, the one-day loss bound at m 1.5 is 10.4% (p99 open risk) to 14.8% (max open risk) of NAV, versus the realized worst day of -5.9% at m 1 (2015-03-25, k 1.05 on 562 bps open) -> -8.9% at m 1.5. All accepted; none of these is a constraint in the rule, they are the disclosure.

changes.name: GRM 1.5 -> 2.0 now, -> 2.25 behind the margin guard and the hedge; 2.5-3.0 only after index legs move to futures and the haircut is measured
changes.rule: GLOBAL_RISK_MULTIPLIER = 2.0 at the next scan cycle. Step to 2.25 when GM-4 (margin guard) is live in order_staging, XS-1 has logged one paper armed episode on the hedge panel, and IBKR what-if margin on the four named historical peak books scaled by 1.5 is under 85% of live NLV. Step past 2.25 only when GM-5 has moved the SPY/QQQ/DIA legs to futures AND MS-2 delivers a measured haircut <= 40% on >= 150 matched fills. Never move GRM more than one step per quarter.
changes.math: GRM_t = 1.5 x min(m_growth, m_margin, m_gap). m_growth = the multiple at which g(m) = E[log(1 + m r_h)] (r_h = r - h x mean r, h = 0.40) is within 1 pt of linear: >= 3 on every window (2016-07+: 21.9/30.4/39.7% at m 1/1.5/2; 2003+: 13.4/19.5/25.4%). m_margin = min over historical stress days d of (NLV_live/750k) x (1 - b) / req_d, b = 10% one-day loss buffer, req_d = requirement/base at m 1: plain PM max day 0.554 -> 1.37 on $632k (2.19 on the p99 day 0.347); the guard (GM-4) replaces the max-day term with the p99 term by construction, giving m 2.19 -> GRM 3.3 ceiling from margin once the guard is live. m_gap = L_1d / (k_999 x OpenRisk_p99) = 0.15 / (1.28 x 0.0544) = 2.15 for an accepted one-day loss of 15% NAV. Binding term today: m_margin without the guard (1.37) -> GRM 2.05; with the guard: min(2.19, 2.15) -> GRM 3.2; the haircut range, not the walls, then holds it at 2.25 until measured.
changes.expected_effect: At GRM 2.25 (m 1.5), h 0.40: ann. log growth +8.5 pts (2016-07+, 21.9 -> 30.4%) / +6.1 pts (2003+, 13.4 -> 19.5%); ann. vol 12.9 -> 19.4%; median 1y maxDD 6.7 -> 9.9% (2016+), 7.2 -> 10.7% (2003+); P(1y DD > 20%) 0 -> 2% / 0 -> 5%; historical-path DD -11.0 -> -15.9% (2016+), -16.4 -> -24.7% (2003+); worst day -4.9 -> -7.4% / -5.9 -> -8.9%. At GRM 2.0: roughly two thirds of each delta. Flat-dollar expectation at h 0.40: ~$150k/yr -> ~$225k/yr on $750k. Cap-fixed realized multiple at m 1.5 is 1.48 (cost ~1 pt of growth, binds on 2% of strategy-signal-days).
changes.confidence: moderate-high on the growth and drawdown arithmetic (four tail models, three windows, two haircuts agree; no cliff in the 2026-07 GRM replay); moderate on the walls (stylized margin rates; must be verified against IBKR what-if before the 2.25 step)
changes.evidence: risk_arch_04_grm_frontier (this lens); unconstrained_growth findings 1-4 and 7; estimation_haircut findings 7-8 (40% central, 27-71%); outside: Thorp 2006 fractional-Kelly identities, MacLean-Thorp-Ziemba 2010, Busseti-Ryu-Boyd 2016, Carver 2015, Suhonen 2017 / McLean-Pontiff 2016 / Harvey-Liu 2015 for the haircut; GRM replay 2026-07-16 (scratch/grm_replay_study.py)
changes.intuition: A book at 7-8% of its honest Kelly is over-insured against a drawdown it says it does not fear; the sizing literature's practitioner floor is 25% of honest Kelly. What actually breaks a book like this is not a 15% drawdown, it is the broker liquidating a 22-leg OLV stack at 15:45 on the day it needs 90% of equity, or one gap day on no-stop legs. Those are step functions and are handled by the guard, the hedge and the stack formula, after which growth theory is allowed to set the number.
changes.risks: Haircut mis-estimated: at h 0.71 the 2003+ historical path at m 1.5 draws down 63%; the two-step path and the MS-2 re-measurement bound this. Broker house-margin uplift (IBKR raised requirements 35% into Nov-2020) turns a feasible book into a forced sale; GM-4 alarms at 85%. The 2026 realized edge per unit risk is 0.52x the ledger; if that is decay rather than midterm base rate, GRM 2.25 is 2.25 x 0.52 of intent, still inside the walls but with lower growth than tabled.
changes.implementation_notes: strategy_config.GLOBAL_RISK_MULTIPLIER (source of truth; scales every nominal bps at import). Aligned: nothing else changes for the constant itself; the per-strategy cap in order_staging.PER_STRAT_DAILY_CAP_BPS / process_signals_fast(cap_bps=250) / build_trade_ledger stays at 250 effective. Log each step with the frontier table and the IBKR what-if numbers in the commit message; re-run risk_arch_04 quarterly and whenever NLV moves 20%.

changes.name: Replace the plan's P(DD > 15%) <= 5% rule with a three-ceiling rule and a quarterly re-derivation
changes.rule: GRM is the largest value satisfying all of: (i) growth: g(m) within 1 pt of linear at the current haircut; (ii) margin: p99 projected requirement day <= 70% of live NLV and max day <= 100% of the sizing base at plain PM rates (rules-based 3x and 30% concentration reported as sensitivities); (iii) gap: k_999 x OpenRisk_p99 x m <= 15% NAV. The drawdown-probability table is DISCLOSED at every step (median, p95, P > 15/20/30% at 1y and 3y, historical path) but is not a constraint.
changes.math: m* = min(m_growth, m_margin, m_gap); GRM = 1.5 m*. Disclosure table from the stationary block bootstrap of the haircut daily series at m*, both vintages plus 2003+, hedged and unhedged (risk_arch_04).
changes.expected_effect: Removes the one a-priori appetite constraint the principal asked to remove (the 5%/15% rule held GRM at 1.5 and is stricter than any practitioner rule); replaces it with the two physical boundaries that can actually end the book. No PnL effect on its own.
changes.confidence: high (rule design; the inputs' confidence is stated under GM-1)
changes.evidence: risk_arch_04; unconstrained_growth recommendation 1; outside: Grossman-Zhou 1993 (drawdown-constrained Kelly costs growth x (1 - alpha) and pays only if drawdown state forecasts, which here it does not: risk_arch_02 dd_gt_5pct fwd21 2.26% vs base 2.34%), Thorp's 1987 jump-risk caveat
changes.intuition: State the walls you can hit, disclose the drawdown you accept, and let growth set the size in between.
changes.risks: A rule with three inputs is only as good as the margin rates it assumes; the IBKR what-if query is the correction.
changes.implementation_notes: Document in CLAUDE.md under Sizing Conventions; scratch/ultracode_sizing_2026-09-02/risk_arch_04_grm_frontier.py + risk_arch_03_stack_stress.py are the recompute scripts; GM-4's guard produces the live requirement numbers.

changes.name: Sizing base: flat $750k until NLV exceeds it, then half-compounding; downside rebase floor at 75% so the flat base cannot lever the book past 1.33x its intended fraction in a drawdown
changes.rule: base_t = 750k while 562.5k <= NLV <= 750k. If NLV < 0.75 x 750k: base_t = NLV / 0.75 (re-set weekly, restored to 750k when NLV recovers above 562.5k). When NLV > 750k: base_t = max(base_{t-1}, 0.5 x 750k + 0.5 x NLV), re-set quarterly, never below the prior quarter. Full compounding only if the measured haircut (MS-2) comes in under 25%.
changes.math: Effective fraction multiple = base/NLV. Today 750/632 = 1.19x intent. The floor caps it at 1/0.75 = 1.33x. Above 750k the half rule gives 10y median terminal 9.0x vs 4.3x flat vs 25.6x full compounding (2016+, no haircut, m 1), 5.6x / 3.5x / 10.2x at 50% haircut and m 1.5, with %-of-peak drawdown unchanged and dollar drawdowns growing at half the full-compounding rate; P(compounding < flat on the same path) 9-24% at 3y in the haircut cells, ~0% at 10y.
changes.expected_effect: No change to today's risk (NLV 632k sits inside the band). Switching to a live-NAV base today would be a 16% risk CUT, not a growth step, and the live-NLV margin ceiling (m 1.34-1.52 on the max day) is already the tighter of the two, so the flat base is kept. The 75% floor is a ruin control that converts the flat base's constant-dollar behaviour into constant-fraction beyond a 25% drawdown; it fires only past the largest drawdown the historical path has produced at GRM 2.25 (-24.7% on 2003+).
changes.confidence: moderate (compounding arithmetic is strong; the floor level is a judgement placed just past the historical path's worst case)
changes.evidence: unconstrained_growth finding 6 (five sizing-base policies, sequencing regret); risk_arch_04 historical-path DDs; risk_arch_02 (negative PnL autocorrelation means the constant-dollar base's up-fraction in drawdowns is not expectancy-negative, so the floor is set for ruin, not for edge)
changes.intuition: Constant dollars on a shrinking account is a martingale; it is fine when losses mean-revert (they do here, acf1 -0.035, acf2 -0.055) and fatal when the account is also the margin. The floor is where the martingale hands over to the broker.
changes.risks: The floor is a drawdown-triggered cut in disguise past -25%; Kaminski-Lo says it costs expectancy on mean-reverting PnL. Accepted: it is sized to fire at most once a decade and the alternative is the broker's cut.
changes.implementation_notes: ACCOUNT_VALUE stays the constant; add a `sizing_base()` helper read by daily_scan sizing and order_staging that applies the band/floor from the nightly /exec-book NLV; engine and ledger stay on the flat basis (the ledger measures edge, not the account). Guard test for the band arithmetic.

changes.name: Margin-feasibility guard in order_staging plus a 15:30 ET headroom check: project the day's requirement on live NLV and scale NEW entries pro rata above 70%
changes.rule: Before submission: Req_proj = sum_open(notional_i x rate_i) + 1.10 x sum_staged(notional_j x rate_j), rates = stock 15%, broad index 8%, small-cap index 10%, 3x ETF 45% (90% for SHORT 3x until the live account's margin report shows PM treatment), sub-$16.67 short stocks at max(30%, $5/share), sub-$5 at 100%. If Req_proj > 0.70 x NLV_live: scale every staged entry's Quantity by (0.70 x NLV - Req_open) / (1.10 x Req_staged), floor 0, and label the row MARGIN_TRIM. If Req_open alone > 0.85 x NLV: email alarm, no new entries. A 15:30 ET check recomputes Req_open on live marks and alarms above 90% of NLV (Soft Edge Margin expires 15:45; MOC exits and the OVS 15:58 EOD-DD sit inside that window).
changes.math: P(requirement > equity within 3y) at m 1.5 on plain PM is 0.1-0.4% unguarded, 7-10% with a 15% equity cushion, 55-73% with a non-broad concentration add-on; at m 2 unguarded 14-23%. The guard converts that absorbing state into a same-day pro-rata haircut on the few days it binds (top-1% requirement days: 42% index ETFs, 58% single stock, 0.2% 3x on my class map; the growth study's finer map puts broad-index at 38% and |net|/gross at 87%, i.e. long clusters, not offsetting shorts).
changes.expected_effect: Removes the forced-liquidation path that is the only true ruin channel between GRM 2 and 3. Cost: trims the book's best days (gross > 100% NAV days are 15% of days and 49% of PnL) on the ~1% of days it binds; unmeasured, needs its own engine replay (a 'MARGIN_TRIM' partial-size row type). Not an ATR-risk cap and not a notional cap: a broker constraint, consistent with the no-notional-caps rule.
changes.confidence: moderate-high that it is needed; moderate on the rates (IBKR TIMS house rules and the concentration trigger are undisclosed)
changes.evidence: risk_arch_03 margin_req_nav_* (plain PM max 0.554 on 2023-02-03, p99 0.347; rules-based 3x max 0.99; conc30 max 0.87); unconstrained_growth finding 3 and recommendation 2; outside: IBKR portfolio-margin mechanics (15%/8%/10%/x3 stress, 110% initial, concentration 30%, SEM expiry 15 minutes before close, auto-liquidation with no call), IBKR Nov-2020 35% house uplift, Jan-2021 300% short requirement on named stocks
changes.intuition: A book with no notional dimension can hold 122% of NAV in one low-ATR ETF; the broker's liquidation is indiscriminate about which strategy's leg it kills, so the plan must trim before the broker does, and it must trim entries, never exits.
changes.risks: The guard fights the flow-aware relief (FL-1) on the same days; order of operations must be cap relief first, then margin trim. Rates drift by broker discretion.
changes.implementation_notes: order_staging.py (OneDrive trading_ibkr): new stage after the per-strategy cap and before the Sheets write; reads /exec-book for open positions and NLV; needs a class map (LEV3X_ALL, INDEX_ETFS, price tiers). Engine parity: add a MARGIN_TRIM partial-size replay in process_signals_fast keyed on reconstructed open notional (risk_arch_03.open_matrix is the reference). Guard test on the four named peak days. Query the IBKR Exposure Fee Calculation Report at current, 1.5x and 2x hypothetical gross via Risk Navigator before the 2.25 step.

changes.name: Route the SPY/QQQ/DIA legs of the dip-buy family through ES/MES/NQ/MNQ futures (precondition for GRM >= 2.5, optional before)
changes.rule: For Weak Close Decent Sznls, Monday Dip, SPY QQQ MonFri Reversion, Indices Oversold Bounce and Monthly Weak Close, when the tradeable ticker is SPY/QQQ/DIA, stage the equivalent futures contracts (MES/MNQ for sub-contract sizes) at the same ATR risk; entry/exit vocabulary unchanged (limit at close - 0.25 ATR, time exits), margin ~5-6% of notional instead of 8%.
changes.math: Index ETFs are 42% of gross on the top-1% requirement days (my map) / 38% (growth study); moving them from 8% to 6% margin lowers the p99 requirement from 0.347 to 0.329 and the max day from 0.554 to 0.551 on my map (the max day is a stock cluster), but on the finer map it lifts the plain-PM wall from m 1.60 to ~2.3 (GRM ~3.5) because its max day (2016-06-14) was an index-ETF cluster. Futures on the exit day also avoid the SEM 15:45 clock for the equity leg.
changes.expected_effect: No expectancy change; relaxes the margin wall on index-cluster days and removes those legs from the concentration-add-on ambiguity (SPY > 50% NAV on 89 days since 2016). Cost: contract granularity (MES = $5 x ES ~ $30k notional) rounds the smallest legs; basis/roll ~2-4 bps per quarter.
changes.confidence: moderate (mechanism is arithmetic; the futures gateway exists in trading_ibkr per the memory notes but the dip-buy limit-entry path is not wired to it)
changes.evidence: risk_arch_03 class_share_of_gross_top1pct_days and open_notional_by_class; unconstrained_growth recommendation 2 (broad-index ETFs 38% of gross on tail days, SPY 89 days > 50% NAV); outside: IBKR broad-index stress 6/8%, futures margin ~5-6%
changes.intuition: The margin wall is built out of low-ATR index ETFs bought in size because the sizing unit is ATR; the same bet in a future needs a third of the equity.
changes.risks: Two execution paths for one strategy family; fills on a -0.25 ATR limit in MES differ from SPY's (tick size, session hours); the beta hedge (XS-1) and these legs must be netted on the hedge panel so the futures book is one line.
changes.implementation_notes: order_staging / eq_order_entry futures branch (trading_ibkr futures gateway design + tests); SPOT_TO_TRADEABLE-style alias map ETF -> contract with multiplier; hedge panel already nets counted equity-index futures. Ship only after GM-4 and XS-1; not required for the GRM 2.25 step.

changes.name: Theme risk budgets: allocate variance share across six themes by shrunk theme Kelly, half-blended, as the envelope inside which the per-strategy tilt (ST-1) operates
changes.rule: Themes: dip_buy_index {MonFri, IOB, Monday Dip, Monthly Weak Close}, dip_buy_stock {WCDS, St OS Sznl}, oversold_hold {OLV, LT Trend ST OS}, short_fade {OVS, 3x ETF Overbot Fade, ATR Ext Gap Up}, bear_etf_fade {3x Bear Fade, 3x Leader Gap Fade}, breakout {52wh, Sector BO}. Theme multiplier M_T = clip(0.5 x w_T + 0.5, 0.75, 1.25) with w_T the shrunk Sigma^-1 mu weight on the theme daily series (Ledoit-Wolf delta 0.3, mu shrunk halfway to equal-Sharpe), expanding window through the prior December, normalised to mean |w| = 1. From the fit through 2026-08 (2010+ / 2016-07+ agreeing on sign): breakout 0.82 / 0.93 -> 0.85; dip_buy_index 1.01 / 1.14 -> 1.10; oversold_hold 1.14 / 1.02 -> 1.10; short_fade 1.00 / 0.94 -> 1.0; dip_buy_stock 0.98 / 1.02 -> 1.0; bear_etf_fade 1.05 / 0.94 -> 1.0. Final per-strategy base-bps multiplier = clip(M_T x m_s, 0.5, 1.5) with m_s from ST-1; OVS stays 1.0 (cap-bound). Re-fit each January; a theme whose w_T stays below 0.6 for two years is a retirement question.
changes.math: w = Sigma_tilde^-1 mu_tilde on the six theme series. Euler variance shares 2010+ (current -> Kelly-implied): dip_buy_index 20.5% -> 21.9%, dip_buy_stock 13.3 -> 12.9, oversold_hold 12.8 -> 21.2, short_fade 19.5 -> 21.4, bear_etf_fade 6.9 -> 9.0, breakout 27.0 -> 13.5; 2016-07+: 16.2 -> 24.4, 13.3 -> 14.6, 16.8 -> 18.4, 27.9 -> 21.5, 10.6 -> 8.8, 15.3 -> 12.3. Breakout owns 37.2% of worst-5%-day loss for 18.4% of PnL (2010+; 25.5% for 11.7% in 2016+) and has the highest variance elasticity (+10% breakout risk -> +5.6% book variance vs +2.7% for oversold_hold). Theme pairwise correlation 0.064 (2010+), effective N 4.44 themes; on the worst 5% of days the average theme correlation is -0.13 and effective N 17: the tail is one theme at a time, not co-movement.
changes.expected_effect: Same direction and roughly the same magnitude as the plan's L1 tilt (52wh 0.73, Sector BO 0.84 cut; OLV 1.29, LT Trend 1.19 raised) but expressed at the level where the tail lives; walk-forward on the strategy tilt already showed PnL/maxDD +18%, 12 of 13 years better, worst year -13% at equal in-sample vol. The theme envelope's own contribution is to stop the strategy tilt from raising IOB and MonFri into the same dip-buy-index bet without a budget (both routes disagree on MonFri) and to keep breakout's variance share near 13-15% rather than 27%.
changes.confidence: moderate (two windows agree on the breakout cut and the dip-buy-index/oversold-hold raise; theme series are the same daily payload the plan's L1 used, so this is a re-aggregation, not independent evidence)
changes.evidence: risk_arch_01_theme_budget (this lens: var/cvar/pnl shares, theme Kelly, tail-day correlation, elasticity); baseline plan L1c-1e (walk-forward gate, tail ownership); estimation_haircut per-strategy keeps; outside: Grinold breadth, Thorp multi-asset Sigma^-1 mu, Jensen-Kelly-Pedersen (rank survives, level does not)
changes.intuition: Six themes at correlation 0.06 is the diversification the book actually has; fifteen strategy names overstate it (two of them are SPY and QQQ on the same day). Budget the six, then split inside each.
changes.risks: Theme membership is a judgement (3x Leader Gap Fade straddles bear-fade and short-fade); the breakout cut lands on the strategy whose recent era is its best (52wh 1.32R in 2022-26 on N 20) and on the momentum factor that the outside evidence calls the most robust post-publication; the 0.75 floor and annual re-fit are the protection. The cut also lowers the book's un-hedged momentum-crash exposure (XS-3), which is a feature.
changes.implementation_notes: Compose with ST-1 in strategy_config as a single `risk_multiplier` per strategy (source of truth, listed in the commit message with both components); daily_scan step 2a and strat_backtester 3b apply it to base bps before every overlay; P3 engine confirmation gate (reproduce >= half the walk-forward gain, maxDD no worse than 1 pt) applies to the composed multipliers. Theme variance shares go on the hedge panel (MS-1).

changes.name: Per-strategy capped half-tilt with the measured per-strategy keep factors as the mu shrinkage (replaces the plan's flat 50% shrink)
changes.rule: m_s = clip(0.5 x w_s + 0.5, 0.6, 1.4), w_s = shrunk Sigma^-1 mu_shrunk on the strategy daily series (expanding window through prior December) where mu_shrunk_s = keep_s x mu_s with keep_s from estimation_haircut_results.json: 3x ETF Fade 0.78, 3x Bear 0.74, ATR Ext 0.73, MonFri 0.72, Monday Dip 0.69, IOB 0.68, Sector BO 0.65, St OS Sznl 0.50, OLV 0.45 (judgement band 0.45-0.60), 3x Leader 0.44, Monthly WC 0.44, LT Trend 0.41, WCDS 0.37, 52wh 0.31 (judgement 0.35-0.50), OVS 0.30 (judgement 0.40-0.55, held at 1.0 anyway). Pilots (N < 30) and OVS stay at 1.0 (ST-2). Composed with TH-1 as clip(M_T x m_s, 0.5, 1.5).
changes.math: Kelly share f_s ~ keep_s x mu_s / sigma_s^2 adjusted for correlation; keep_s = selection x realized-2026 x survivorship x cost. The plan's fit through 2025 gave 52wh 0.73, IOB 0.83, Sector BO 0.84, WCDS 0.84, St OS 0.92, Monday Dip 1.02, ATR Ext 1.04, 3x ETF 1.15, MonFri 1.16, LT Trend 1.19, OLV 1.29; with keep_s in the mean the ordering holds but LT Trend and OLV are tempered toward ~1.10-1.15 and MonFri/IOB rise toward 1.2 / 0.9 (index strategies with 5 versions and no survivorship).
changes.expected_effect: Walk-forward (plan L1d, flat shrink): PnL +4 pts NAV/yr, Sharpe 2.05 -> 2.15, PnL/maxDD +18%, 12 of 13 years better, worst year -13%. Keep-weighted variant not walked forward here; expected to give up ~1 pt of the raise on OLV/LT Trend and recover it on MonFri; adopt only if the P3 engine gate passes with the composed multipliers.
changes.confidence: moderate (plan's gate passed; the keep factors are a transparent formula, not a fitted model, and both estimators bracket 0.60 at the book level)
changes.evidence: baseline plan L1a-1e and P3; estimation_haircut findings 3, 4, 7, 9 and recommendation 2; outside: Harvey-Liu nonlinear haircut (t > 3 lightly, t ~ 2 heavily), Baker-McHale shrinkage alpha = t^2/(t^2+1), Chopra-Ziemba (errors in means cost 20x errors in covariances)
changes.intuition: The two things a Kelly allocator must distrust most in this book are the left tail of a small sample (IOB's -7.2R, St OS Sznl's -6.8R) and a mean that was tuned 17-51 times on the full history (52wh, WCDS, OVS). The keep factors put the second distrust into the same formula as the first.
changes.risks: keep_s is dominated by the 2026 partial year for OLV and LT Trend (P(2026 mean < half trailing) 0.96 / 0.84), which is also the midterm base rate; the tilt caps at 1.4 and the 2027 Q1 re-read (HC-1) is the correction.
changes.implementation_notes: One `risk_multiplier` per strategy in strategy_config (composed TH-1 x ST-1); daily_scan 2a / strat_backtester 3b; annual January re-fit script in scratch (dynamic_sizing_study4 pattern with keep_s applied to mu); P3 engine confirmation before go-live; commit message carries the table.

changes.name: Pilots and low-N strategies: mean capped at 0.5x ledger, risk budget 25-40% of the family's mature bps, stepping up on trade count
changes.rule: 3x Leader Gap Fade (N 24), Monthly Weak Close (N 14), and any strategy or overlay with N < 30 conditional trades: sizing mean = 0.5 x ledger avgR; base bps <= 0.4 x the family's mature-strategy bps until 30 trades; 0.5x at 50 trades AND episode-clustered t > 2; 0.75x at 100 trades and t > 2.5; full at t > 3 or a pre-registered LOYO floor. 3x Bear Fade (one-regime sample, 2020+) stays at 25 bps nominal until it has traded a second bear regime.
changes.math: At n 30, avgR 0.5, sd 1.5: t 1.78, 95% CI on per-trade Sharpe [-0.03, 0.70]; n 50 t 2.29; n 100 t 3.24. Harvey-Liu haircuts approach 100% at marginal t under multiple testing; Bailey-LdP MinBTL says a handful of variants on 3-5 years of data produce in-sample Sharpe ~1 by luck. Monthly Weak Close's per-trade SR of 3.5 at N 14 is not a believable number.
changes.expected_effect: No live change today (both pilots run at pilot bps: 25 / 30 nominal); prevents TH-1/ST-1 from raising either on an unbelievable point estimate.
changes.confidence: high
changes.evidence: estimation_haircut recommendation 6; outside base-rate pack (b): 60-80% haircut for < 30-trade pilots, launch-timing decay (Brightman 2015, Huang-Song-Xiang 2024, arXiv 2604.18821)
changes.intuition: A strategy added because its recent cell looked exceptional decays worst; every pilot in this book is by definition recent.
changes.risks: Slows a genuine new edge's scale-up by ~2 years; accepted.
changes.implementation_notes: strategy_config execution `pilot: True` flag that ST-1's re-fit script reads (excluded from the tilt, mean capped); document the step-up schedule in CLAUDE.md.

changes.name: OVS bottom-extremity cut: 0.5x when the mean of rank_ret_2d/5d/10d/21d is below 94
changes.rule: mult = 0.5 if mean(rank_2d, rank_5d, rank_10d, rank_21d) < 94 else 1.0; composes multiplicatively with path, cycle mult, scale-out and both caps; no top-tier boost. Ship after an engine replay with the caps re-applied.
changes.math: Cell < 94: N 392, avgR +0.17, win 0.59; >= 94: N 878, avgR +0.47, win 0.71; mu/sigma^2 ratio 3.1x. Episode-clustered t +5.38 (217 episodes), LOYO 80% of 20 years, holds in both tiers, both gap paths, all four eras; multivariate t +2.60 independent of the T+1 gap (t +5.18) and signal density (t +5.44). Threshold sweep 93-96: 17-18 of 24 years better.
changes.expected_effect: On equal total OVS risk: +12.9% R per unit risk (0.298 -> 0.337), 17 of 24 years better, daily sd x1.06, worst year -$13.9k (2020). If not redeployed: -$36k over 24 years of $607k OVS PnL for a 33% smaller staged-risk footprint. Walk-forward tercile form: +19.7% PnL, 13 of 18 years. Freed cap room flows to higher-extremity rows on cluster days (ST-4, FL-1).
changes.confidence: moderate-high
changes.evidence: signal_quality finding 1 and recommendation 1; not a P(win) selectivity trap: win rate and expectancy move together here (+0.12 win, +0.30R) and the mechanism is that reversal scales with the prior move
changes.intuition: A vol-spike fade is paid in proportion to how far the spike overshot; the bottom third barely spiked.
changes.risks: Cut-point 94 and multiplier 0.5 were chosen after seeing the tercile table; the walk-forward version is the clean check. Midterm years flatten the gradient.
changes.implementation_notes: daily_scan reads the same rank_ret_* columns the filter evaluates (sizing step 2c-style overlay); strat_backtester 3b replays PIT from the same columns; guard test; engine replay with 250 cap + P2 cap before ship.

changes.name: OVS path-2 aggregate daily cap 0.75% -> 1.5% nominal (1.125% -> 2.25% effective); per-strategy cap unchanged
changes.rule: strategy_config OVS execution path2_daily_cap_pct: 0.75 -> 1.5. order_staging reads the row stamp (Path2_Daily_Cap_Pct); engine replays.
changes.math: 202 of 609 P2 trades were capped; capped avgR +0.37 vs uncapped +0.18 (capping lands on cluster days). Uncapping to full 12 bps effective: +$49.5k over 24y (+8.1% of OVS PnL), worst single-day extra loss -$1.4k, best +$11.9k, positive in 11 of 14 capping years.
changes.expected_effect: +$25-50k over 24y depending on how often the doubled cap still binds; worst extra day bounded at -$1.4k because the per-strategy 250 cap (and FL-1's 375 relief) still governs the day.
changes.confidence: moderate (cluster-year concentrated; engine replay is the confirmation)
changes.evidence: signal_quality finding 3 and recommendation 2; within_strategy_adds finding 5 (P1 cluster legs are OVS's best; P2 doubling everywhere is NOT supported: 0.280 vs 0.298, so only the cap moves, not P2 base bps)
changes.intuition: The P2 cap trims the mild-gap rows on exactly the days the mild gap is a crowd, not a fluke.
changes.risks: More P2 shares on the short-squeeze days (2021-01-27 type); bounded by the strategy cap and the scale-out.
changes.implementation_notes: Aligned: strategy_config (source), daily_scan stamps Path2_Daily_Cap_Pct, order_staging P2 aggregate stage, strat_backtester P2 cap replay, build_trade_ledger; tests/test_ovs_scaleout.py style guard.

changes.name: Stack and clone risk budget as a theme one-day loss formula (binds past the p99, never as a per-leg variance tax)
changes.rule: For each theme T, new legs may be added at full marginal-edge size until OpenRisk_T x k_999,T x m > L_T, with L_T = 8% of the sizing base per theme (book-level: OpenRisk_book x 1.28 x m <= 15%). Beyond the bound, new legs scale into the remaining room (pro rata, floor 0); existing legs are never trimmed (exits are the strategy's own rules, the vol-confirm exit for OLV, the time stop everywhere). k_999,T from risk_arch_03: dip_buy_index 2.61, dip_buy_stock 2.75, oversold_hold 1.50, short_fade 2.40, breakout 1.38, book 1.28. Implied open-risk ceilings at m 1.5 (in current-size bps of the base): dip_buy_index 204, dip_buy_stock 194, oversold_hold 356, short_fade 222, breakout 386, book 781. No rho, sector, same-ticker or leg-count term anywhere.
changes.math: loss_bound(T) = k_q(T) x OpenRisk_T x m with k = realized theme day loss / open ATR risk, q = 99.9th pct over 2005+ days with >= 50 bps open. Compare: oversold_hold open risk p99 265 bps, max 699 (2025-01-14, the 22-leg OLV stack); short_fade p99 284, max 715 (2023-02-03); breakout p99 405, max 495; dip_buy_index p99 150, max 285; dip_buy_stock p99 192, max 302. So the formula binds past the p99 for every theme except breakout (where the ceiling sits between p99 and max) and the plan's rejected 250-400 bps OLV caps (which bound at p90-p95 and cost $28-70k/16y) are NOT re-created: the OLV stack of 2025-01-10 (22 legs, 439 bps open, k 0.55) is untouched; the 2025-01-14 peak (699 bps) is trimmed to 356 in m 1 units = 533 bps effective at GRM 2.25, i.e. the last ~5 legs of one stack, once in 21 years. OLV's deep stacks actually lose LESS per unit open risk (k p99 0.61 at 7+ legs vs 1.00 at 2-3), which is why the edge lens, not the variance lens, governs adds.
changes.expected_effect: Expectancy cost near zero (a handful of legs in 21 years, each in a cell whose avgR is above the strategy's mean); one-day loss at GRM 2.25 bounded at 8% per theme / 15% book against a realized worst of -8.9% (2015-03-25 scaled). This is the formula that lets every add rule below (AD-2..AD-5, FL-1, FL-2) size UP on marginal expected R without an open-ended tail.
changes.confidence: moderate-high that the bound is the right object (k is stable: book p99 0.91, p99.9 1.28, max 1.86, and abs loss scales with open risk at elasticity 0.72); moderate on the 8%/15% levels (appetite numbers placed just past the realized worst day)
changes.evidence: risk_arch_03_stack_stress (this lens); within_strategy_adds findings 1-4 and 8 (adds are the higher-edge legs; Kelly-concurrency and sqrt-n budgets lose at equal risk: OLV 0.651/0.678 vs 0.790); baseline plan L2 (OLV sleeve caps 250-400 rejected, -$70k/16y); outside: Busseti-Ryu-Boyd (bound the tail per unit of growth, not the variance), Thorp's jump-risk caveat, Ang-Chen downside-correlation asymmetry in the past-loser cell
changes.intuition: A stack is one bet with rising per-leg edge; the right budget on one bet is the worst day it can hand you, not the number of tickets. Put the formula where it only ever fires on the day the book would otherwise be the broker's.
changes.risks: Open risk counts filled legs; up to three days of unfilled OLV limits are invisible to both engine and scan (the T+3 window), so the live check should include working entries. If k drifts up (a new gap regime), the bound tightens automatically only after the day it should have fired.
changes.implementation_notes: daily_scan sizing post-pass (after 5c): recompute OpenRisk_T from open positions + working entries via the ticker-cap loader machinery (load_open_position_notionals pattern, keyed on Risk_Amt and theme); scale new rows; stamp `TailBudget_Mult` in Sizing notes; strat_backtester replays from open_positions state the way the OLV ticker cap does (fraction-of-sizing-equity terms so flat and compounded passes agree); build_trade_ledger aligned; guard test with the 2025-01-14 and 2023-02-03 days. Theme map lives in strategy_config.

changes.name: OLV signal-recency ladder re-keyed to max(ticker-recency rung, sleeve-depth rung)
changes.rule: mult = max(recency_rung(ticker, 21 td: 0.5 / 0.7 / 1.0 by prior own-ticker signal days), depth_rung(n_open_OLV_legs incl. working entries: 0.5 at 0 open, 0.7 at 1-2, 1.0 at 3+)); composes with the earnings override, frag/PC bands and the ticker notional cap as today; same-ticker adds stay full size.
changes.math: Current ladder halves 81% of solo legs (avgR 0.48) but also 43-49% of legs entered into 3+ open OLV names (0.93-1.15R). Replay 2005-2026: current $418k PnL / 0.790 PnL per $ risk / exit-basis worst-21d -$14.0k; depth-OR-ticker $543k / 0.820 / -$13.4k, exit maxDD -$19.6k vs -$20.6k, +$16k at equal risk, PnL/risk >= current in 15 of 20 years; MTM maxDD -$54.1k vs -$40.6k because the footprint grows 25% (-$43.3k at equal risk). OLV open-leg count hi vs lo: 0.849R vs 0.336R, t 3.12, positive in 94% of years.
changes.expected_effect: +$125k/21y raw, +$16k at equal risk, better realized worst-21d; the appetite cut stays on the weak (isolated) cell. With AD-1 the footprint growth has a written ceiling.

changes.name: Weak Close Decent Sznls and LT Trend ST OS: solo 0.75x / adds 1.25x
changes.rule: mult = 0.75 if n_open_{strategy} == 0 (filled + working) else 1.25; same-sector and same-ticker clusters explicitly NOT cut; composes with WCDS's frag/PC bands, the L1 tilt and the 250 cap.
changes.math: WCDS same-day adds 0.73R (N 75, t 2.7, LOYO 2.1, bootstrap P 0.021) vs solo 0.21R (156); per signal day 1 fill 0.14R ($579/day) vs 4-5 fills 0.93R ($14.4k/day). Replay: $337k -> $362k on 5% less risk, PnL/risk 0.281 -> 0.317, +$43k at equal risk, MTM maxDD -$60.8k -> -$55.1k; cap binds on 9 of 194 days at 1.25x. changes.confidence: moderate
changes.evidence: within_strategy_adds finding 6 and recommendations 3-4; flow_conditional finding 1 (dip_buy and oversold_hold flow is a size-UP state)

changes.implementation_notes: Generic `open_count_ladder` execution field (the dormant ladder_multipliers machinery with a per-strategy key, counting open + working); daily_scan + strat_backtester + tests; fold the LT dial-cell result into the P2 exemption re-test (RG-2).

changes.name: 52wh Breakout 0.5x at >= 6 open legs (tail insurance; replaces the plan's >= 5)
changes.rule: mult = 0.5 if n_open_52wh >= 6 else 1.0; labelled tail insurance with a re-exam at +15 legs in the cell; retire if the cell's avgR >= 0.4 then.
changes.math: Exact-5 open: 1.71R (N 13, $87.6k); >= 6: 0.08R (N 23) 2010+ but 0.92R pre-2010 (N 17); full-history >= 6 vs rest -0.10R, bootstrap P 0.57. The Feb-2014 worst 21-day window (-$59.5k) is 88% deep-stack legs. Replays: >= 5 at 0.5x -$68.5k raw / -$9.4k equal risk (cuts the 1.71R cell); >= 6 at 0.5x -$34.6k raw (nearly all pre-2010), +$7.5k equal risk, sleeve worst-21d -$59.5k -> -$33.3k, MTM maxDD -$78k -> -$61k.

changes.confidence: low on the cell (era-dependent, 4 post-2010 episodes), moderate that the insurance is cheap
changes.evidence: within_strategy_adds finding 7 and recommendation 5; risk_arch_01 (breakout cvar5 share 0.372, variance elasticity 0.056); baseline plan decision #3 (re-thresholded)
changes.intuition: The sixth simultaneous breakout is a late-cycle condition; nothing about depth in this strategy is stable enough to be an edge rule, so call it what it is.
changes.risks: Cuts a leg that pre-2010 was 0.92R; the equal-risk cost says the price is small.
changes.implementation_notes: Same open_count_ladder field as AD-3 with breaks [6] and mults [1.0, 0.5]; written trigger in CLAUDE.md.

changes.name: Clones: IOB SPY+QQQ same-day pairs at 0.5x each; extend the cross-strategy same-ticker clamp to every dip-buy pair; MonFri SPY+QQQ untouched
changes.rule: Within Indices Oversold Bounce, when SPY and QQQ fire the same day each leg sizes at 0.5x (Rung 3 at rho ~ 1: f = mu / sigma^2 (1 + rho)). CROSS_STRATEGY_OVERLAP_OVERRIDES extended to Monday Dip + WCDS, MonFri + WCDS, Monthly Weak Close + MonFri (20 bps nominal each side, GRM-scaled, staged-signal keyed). MonFri's own SPY+QQQ days are its best days (3.1x PnL at 2.1x sd) and stay full.
