Fourteen same-day same-ticker cross-strategy pairs since 2010 with R corr 0.97; only IOB + MonFri clamped today.
changes.expected_effect: Variance-only: removes doubled tickets with no expected-value content.
changes.confidence: high (a rho = 1 clamp has no expectancy content to be wrong about)
changes.evidence: baseline plan L2 decisions #1, #2, #13
changes.intuition: Two tickets on one horse is size, not diversification; where the second ticket carries more edge (MonFri), Kelly says keep it.
changes.risks: None in expectation.
changes.implementation_notes: strategy_config CROSS_STRATEGY_OVERLAP_OVERRIDES entries + a within-strategy variant keyed on (strategy, signal date) for IOB; daily_scan 5b; strat_backtester 3b3c candidate pre-pass; existing guard tests extended.

changes.name: Flow-aware per-strategy daily cap: 250 -> 375 bps effective on days the family's trailing-5d raw candidate count is in its top tercile (dip_buy, oversold_hold, short_fade); breakout unchanged; never removed
changes.rule: cap_bps(strategy, day) = 375 if family_flow5(day) >= threshold else 250, thresholds dip_buy >= 6, oversold_hold >= 7, short_fade >= 104 candidates (raw filter masks BEFORE earnings blackout / T+1 gates, counted from the same masks daily_scan evaluates). Order of operations: cap relief, then GM-4 margin trim. x99 (removal) is forbidden.
changes.math: Cap binds on 20.9% of trades (130 strategy-days) and on the top-flow tercile at 78% for short_fade (mean scale 0.38), 26% oversold_hold, 12% dip_buy; cap-bound OVS avgR 0.62 vs 0.20 unbound. Relief x1.5 replay 2010-2026: book PnL +3.8% (+$132k), risk +2.0%, PnL/risk 0.491 -> 0.499, Sharpe 2.199 -> 2.222, maxDD -$92,866 vs -$92,867 and worst-21d byte-identical, 10 of 17 years better and 7 identical. Full removal: short_fade Sharpe 1.18 -> 0.93, maxDD -$44k -> -$127k. Within-strategy proxy for OVS alone (P1 x1.5 at depth >= 6): +$92k/23y, PnL/risk 0.298 -> 0.327, worst day -$26k -> -$35k (2021-01-27).
changes.expected_effect: +~$8k/yr at Sharpe up and identical tails on the family replay; the OVS proxy shows the one day the cap exists for (2021-01-27) widens ~35% if relief lands on it, which the x1.5 (not x99) form bounds.
changes.confidence: moderate-high (unfitted rule, thresholds from pre-2010 data, mechanical mechanism)
changes.evidence: flow_conditional finding 6 and recommendation 1; within_strategy_adds finding 5; signal_quality finding 2 (cap-bound days carry risk-weighted avgR 0.84 vs 0.41); seasonality_flow finding 5 (OVS 5+ signal days avgR 0.65 vs 0.23, q 0.002, LOYO floor +0.335)
changes.intuition: The cap is a scalar throttle on exactly the days the mean-reverting families are paid; keep it as tail insurance and let it breathe when the tape is the trade.
changes.risks: Verify live placed totals against the ledger's implied ones first (the ledger only sees filled risk); relief on the short-squeeze day is the cost.
changes.implementation_notes: order_staging PER_STRAT_DAILY_CAP_BPS becomes a per-day function reading a `Family_Flow5` stamp daily_scan writes on every row (count from filters.live_signal_mask over the family's strategies); engine cap post-pass uses the same count from the candidate list; build_trade_ledger aligned; tests for the three thresholds and the x99 prohibition.

changes.name: Up-only family flow multiplier 1.25x on base bps for the three mean-reverting families; dip_buy gated to dial < 50
changes.rule: New sizing step after 2b (frag band) and before 2c (recency ladder): mult = 1.25 when family_flow5 >= threshold (dip_buy >= 6 AND 10d-MA 63d dial < 50; oversold_hold >= 7; short_fade >= 104), else 1.0. No breakout carrier. The 0.75x low-flow leg is NOT adopted (it costs 5.7% PnL for 9.1% less risk; the brief does not need variance funding). Post-ship review pre-registered: PnL/risk on the first 60 hi-flow trades >= 1.3x the concurrent lo/mid-flow trades, else retire.
changes.math: Flow terciles: dip_buy avgR 0.216 / 0.657 / 0.569 (PnL per risk 0.212 -> 0.572), episode-cluster t 2.70; oversold_hold 0.317 / 0.571 / 0.855, t 3.00; short_fade 0.298 / 0.367 / 0.678, t 3.21; per-year Spearman positive in 82-84% of 22 years; survives VIX, SPY-trend, realized-vol, drawdown and dial controls (t barely moves); inside dial >= 30 the dip_buy effect is absent (+0.03R, t 0.1), hence the gate. Up-only replay 2010-2026 with cap re-applied: book PnL +5.0% at +4.2% risk, Sharpe 2.197 (flat), maxDD -$92.9k -> -$102.8k, 17 of 17 years better, worst year +1%; combined with FL-1: +9.9% PnL, +6.8% risk, Sharpe 2.224, maxDD -$102.8k, 17/17.
changes.expected_effect: +~$10k/yr on the flat basis; a growth/PnL-per-risk lever, not a Sharpe lever (high-flow legs are one correlated bet). AD-1 bounds the stack it builds.
changes.confidence: moderate (expectancy evidence strong; Sharpe-neutral by construction; exactly the appetite decision the brief invites)
changes.evidence: flow_conditional findings 1-5 and recommendation 2; seasonality_flow finding 5; outside: Nagel 2012 (liquidity-provision premium scales with stress), Daniel-Moskowitz loser-decile up-betas
changes.intuition: When many setups fire together the market is paying for liquidity; the crowded-selloff reading is wrong-signed for this book in every mean-reverting family.
changes.risks: Rule is Sharpe-neutral and adds maxDD ~10% at equal risk in the two-sided form; the up-only form adds risk on the correlated days, which is what AD-1 and FL-1's x1.5 bound are for.
changes.implementation_notes: daily_scan sizing step 2b2 with the same Family_Flow5 stamp as FL-1; strat_backtester 3b replay from the candidate list; composes with OLV ladder (first-iteration OLV on a hi-flow day = 0.5 x 1.25); tests; CLAUDE.md records the closed negative on the down-side leg and on breakouts.

changes.name: Dial-armed WHOLE-BOOK beta hedge (P1) promoted to paper-track-then-ship with amendments: threshold 50/45, 126d shrunk beta, ES/MES, 1.0x, whole-book target
changes.rule: armed_t = hysteresis(dial_lag1 >= 50 arm, < 45 release) on the live 10d-MA 63d series (PIT vintage primary for scoring). beta_hat = 126-session lag-1 OLS of the flat-basis book MTM on SPY (or 0.5 x 63d + 0.5 x expanding shrunk), clipped [-1, 2], refreshed daily. MES contracts = beta_hat x sizing_base / (5 x ES price); ES for the bulk. Native MOC entry per the 2026-08-21 encoding rule; release fully when dial < 45; hedge ratio never above 1.0x; instrument never NQ or RTY. Ship after one paper armed episode logged on the hedge panel.
changes.math: Optimal index position with a costless future: w_m = mu_m / sigma_m^2 - beta' w_idio; at dial >= 65 the conditional SPY mean is -24% ann (live) / -8% (PIT) so the term flips sign and the optimum is to short the embedded beta; a scalar cut shrinks the idiosyncratic Kelly book by the same factor as the factor it wanted to remove. My replay (risk_arch_04, 126d beta, 2 bps per arm): live 2016-07+ 392 armed days, hedge +4.5% NAV, Sharpe 2.775 -> 2.847, maxDD -8.32 -> -7.89%, worst-21d -6.30 -> -5.24%, CVaR1 -2.44 -> -2.43%, armed-day Sharpe 1.84 -> 2.27; PIT 2018+ 544 armed days, hedge +14.5% NAV, Sharpe 2.90 -> 3.07, maxDD -8.32 -> -7.89%, worst-21d -6.30 -> -5.24%, armed Sharpe 1.85 -> 2.61. Cross-strategy study: PIT 50/45 13 episodes, 10 positive, clustered t 1.68, bootstrap P(<= 0) 0.046, placebo rank 1.000, LOYO 7 of 9; 65/60 is t 0.99 on PIT and lives on Feb-2020. On the frontier at m 1.5 / h 0.40 the hedge moves the historical-path DD from -15.9% to -14.3% (live) and P(1y DD > 15%) 11% -> 10%: a modest tail improvement whose main value is turning the dial's forecast into PnL and keeping the book's convexity (beta_up 0.79 vs beta_down 0.26 at dial 65+) instead of cutting it.
changes.expected_effect: ~1.3 episodes/yr, ~+$8k per episode on the flat basis, +0.07 to +0.17 full-sample Sharpe, false-alarm carry ~-$5k/yr; worst-21d improves ~1 pt of NAV in both vintages.
changes.confidence: moderate (passes the pre-registered PIT ship rule with margin on t; 13 episodes; drift-driven)
changes.evidence: risk_arch_04 hedge block (this lens); cross_strategy_regime findings 1, 3, 4, 6 and recommendations 1, 3, 5; baseline plan L3 and P1; cycle_macro finding 4 (dial is orthogonal to vol regimes, so nothing double-counts); outside: Daniel-Moskowitz (ex-ante beta hedges of state-dependent-beta strategies fail; the fix is a bear-state indicator, which is what the dial is), Longin-Solnik (correlation rises with bear trend, not vol)
changes.intuition: The dial does not move the book's variance; it moves how much of the book is one market bet and what that bet's drift is. The only control that acts on that quantity is a factor position with the sign the dial chose.
changes.risks: Signal definitions are today's code (PIT cures weight lookahead only); the daily payload ends 2026-08-07 so Aug-2026 is truncated; 63d betas have zero predictive correlation exactly when armed (use 126d/shrunk); futures margin adds on top of the equity requirement (GM-4 must count it).
changes.implementation_notes: Hedge panel (execution.js) already computes MES/ES target arithmetic display-only; add the arming state machine + beta_126 in scripts/build_betas.py output (book beta series from strategy_daily), the paper log, and an `event_moo`-style native-MOC placer gated by a flag; roll on the panel's schedule; log every arm/release with beta_126, beta_63, armed-day SPY drift to date.

changes.name: Second-stage hedge sensitivity, pre-registered now: arming gate dial >= 50 AND VIX < 20, forced release at VIX >= 30 (or dial < 45)
changes.rule: Adopt only if it is not worse than plain 50/45 across the next two out-of-sample armed episodes. Decision rule fixed before the next episode.
changes.math: PIT: plain +$104k t 1.68 vs gate + release at 30: +$129k t 2.03, Sharpe 2.90 -> 3.06; live +$58k t 0.97 vs +$35k t 0.72. Found after inspecting 12 variants: every t here is inflated by about one unit.
changes.expected_effect: Removes the hedge in the post-spike phase where the book's beta collapses (0.17 at VIX 30+) and its edge peaks (Sharpe 3.8); expected to trim false-alarm cost, not add PnL.
changes.confidence: low (in-sample refinement)
changes.evidence: cross_strategy_regime finding 8 and recommendation 4; finding 2 (beta is highest in low-VIX near-the-highs tape, lowest after vol arrives)
changes.intuition: The dip-buys want the selloff once it has arrived; the hedge should already be off by then.
changes.risks: Selection over 12 variants; hence prereg, not ship.
changes.implementation_notes: Add to the P1 protocol text; the panel logs VIX at arm/release so the out-of-sample scoring is automatic.

changes.name: Hedge target and residual-factor display: whole book (never FAMILY4 + OLV); the covariance carriers at high dial are oversold_hold and breakout; show the momentum-factor loading the SPY hedge does not cover
changes.rule: Target series for beta = flat-basis total book MTM. If a partial target is ever wanted for operational reasons, define it as {OLV, LT Trend ST OS, 52wh Breakout, St OS Sznl}. Display on the hedge panel: per-theme share of SPY covariance while armed, the book's 12-1 momentum-factor loading, and effective N of themes.
changes.math: Live dial 65+ (133 days): SPY-covariance shares oversold_hold 43%, breakout 31%, short_fade 12%, dip_buy_index 8%; theme variance shares oversold_hold 35%, short_fade 33%, breakout 18%; Sharpe breakout -2.14, dip_buy_stock -1.93 while armed. PIT 65+ (299 days): book beta 0.36, R2 0.17, oversold_hold beta 0.15 (highest), variance share 37%. Sub-book (FAMILY4 + MWC + 3x Bear + OLV) is 15.6% of book variance and beta 0.11 at 65+ while the rest carries 0.30; the sub-book hedge earns a third to two thirds of the whole-book hedge. Momentum factor: book loading 0.10 (t 2.7) at dial >= 50, ~15% of book variance at high dial, carriers OLV / 52wh / LTT / 3x Fade.
changes.expected_effect: Correct target roughly doubles the hedge's PnL per unit of operational cost; the momentum display makes the un-hedged momentum-crash exposure visible before the hedge is placed (a 2009-03-style rebound hits the breakout and OLV legs through the factor, not through SPY).
changes.confidence: moderate (covariance shares are partly who-holds-what by regime, which is what the hedge must cover)
changes.evidence: risk_arch_01 by_dial_bucket (this lens); cross_strategy_regime findings 5-6 and recommendations 3, 6; baseline plan L3 per-strategy daily table (52wh Sharpe -2.2 at >= 50)
changes.intuition: At high dial the factor migrates out of the family the bands already cut and into the trend dip-buy and the breakouts; hedge where the beta is.
changes.risks: Momentum factor is built on survivors; use its loadings, not its mean.
changes.implementation_notes: scripts/build_betas.py: add book/theme betas and the momentum loading (cross_strategy_regime_mom_factor.parquet method); execution.js hedge panel rows; no order logic.

changes.name: Keep the FAMILY4 / 3x Bear / Monthly Weak Close frag bands and the P/C-fear tables as they are; pre-register re-opening the 0.25x/zero cell on HEDGED returns once XS-1 is live
changes.rule: No change now. Prereg: once the hedge has two live armed episodes, re-score the family's dial >= 50 cell on beta-hedged trade returns (PIT weights, episode-clustered, LOYO); a decision rule (e.g. restore 0.5x at dial >= 50 when fear ON) is written before the run.
changes.math: FAMILY4 PIT gate: hi -0.10R vs lo +0.63R, clustered t -1.96, negative in 6 of 9 years (the cut's evidence). The book at dial 65+ has beta_up 0.79 vs beta_down 0.26: a cut removes that convexity, a hedge keeps it. The outside base rate (Nagel: liquidity-provision Sharpe rises with VIX) argues for the fear-ON branch the P/C tables already carry (full size in washout) and against the OFF-state zero as a default; the repo's PIT result is the book-specific override and is not overturned here.
changes.expected_effect: None now; flags the one place where the cut and the hedge act on the same state and the evidence for the cut is one notch stronger than for the hedge.
changes.confidence: low on the eventual outcome; high that it is the right test
changes.evidence: cross_strategy_regime recommendation 7 and finding 4; cycle_macro finding 4 (bands and vol-state act on disjoint days); PC fear-band prereg 2026-08-05; outside: Nagel 2012, CFM hidden-beta-in-dip-trades 2024 (dip-buy returns are largely drift), Longin-Solnik
changes.intuition: Cutting the family at fragile highs and hedging the book's beta at fragile highs are two answers to one question; find out which one the hedged returns want.
changes.risks: Re-opening a shipped appetite decision; the prereg discipline is the guard.
changes.implementation_notes: Prereg doc beside family_pc_fear_band_prereg_2026-08-05.md; needs an engine rerun with frag bands off (the pcfear shadow parquet is the partial precedent).

changes.name: Run P2 (exemption re-test) at the 50 line on PIT weights; LT Trend ST OS [[50, 999, 0.5]] is the one candidate; OLV and OVS stay exempt; fold in the LT adds-vs-solo split
changes.rule: frag_risk_bands for LT Trend ST OS = [[50, 999, 0.5]] (plain table, not P/C-conditioned) if the prereg gate holds on the live PIT series: clustered t <= -2.0 (have -2.33, 9 episodes), survives drop-best-episode (have -0.34), LOYO all negative (have -0.48..-0.28). Apply the band to SOLO and 1-2-open LT legs only if the adds split replicates (adds 0.63R at 65+ vs solo -0.12R). Re-exam at +2 hi-dial episodes; retire if episode sign count falls below 5/11.
changes.math: LT Trend PIT >= 50: 0.107R (N 62) vs 0.482 (N 87), diff -0.375; WF 2019+: PPR +14%, 5 of 6 years, strategy Sharpe 1.00 -> 1.14, maxDD -2.25 -> -1.43; book Sharpe +0.01, +$47k risk-matched over 8y. Book [65, 999) on PIT: +0.006R vs < 50 (t 0.04); OLV [65, 999) PIT +0.235R (t 1.20); OVS P1 [50, 999) -0.104 (t -0.84). The plan's current-weights '65+ book avgR halves' cell is lookahead-inflated and is dropped.
changes.expected_effect: Small in dollars; removes the one exemption that fails on PIT. Correct the plan's L3 narrative to the PIT table.
changes.confidence: moderate-low (5 of 9 episodes negative; 2021 and 2026 carry 28 of 62 trades)
changes.evidence: cycle_macro finding 5 and recommendations 3-4; signal_quality finding 5 (dial gradients on the current-weights vintage vanish on PIT: OLV +1.16/+0.78/+0.49 -> +1.22/+0.67/+0.98); within_strategy_adds finding 6 (LT adds x dial)
changes.intuition: An intermediate-term uptrend dip-buy is the strategy most exposed to a fragile-at-highs distribution rolling over; its solo legs are the exposure, its cluster adds are the washout.
changes.risks: PIT weights only cure calibration lookahead; signal definitions are today's code.
changes.implementation_notes: P2 protocol text updated to the 50 line and PIT; strategy_config frag_risk_bands for LT Trend; tests/test_frag_risk_bands.py; every future dial-conditioned within-strategy claim must be scored on the PIT series (MS-2).

changes.name: OLV market-state tilt (prereg, half-tilt): 1.25x when SPY closes 3-10% below its 252d high at the signal close; at-highs side untouched
changes.rule: execution['market_state_bands'] for Oversold Low Volume: SPY close / rolling-252d high - 1 in [-0.10, -0.03) -> 1.25x (fitted value 1.5x; half-tilt shipped), else 1.0x; composes with the ladder, earnings override and ticker cap; engine replays from master_prices point-in-time. Ship rule: clustered t >= 1.5 on 2010+ AND >= 10 of 15 WF years better (both currently met); no cut on the < 3% side.
changes.math: OLV x spy_dd 3-10: avgR 1.184 (N 103) vs 0.554 rest, t 2.98, 8 pos / 1 neg years, survives Size_Mult >= 0.99 and dial < 50 subsets; single-strategy WF 2010-2026 PPR 0.796 -> 0.885 (+11.3%), 11 of 15 years, OLV Sharpe 1.33 -> 1.36, maxDD -2.75 -> -2.33; fixed 1.5x: 16 of 17 years, book Sharpe 2.515 -> 2.553, maxDD -8.17 -> -8.09, +$74k risk-matched. Cutting the < 3% side costs -$18k risk-matched (the cell is still +0.56R): do not.
changes.expected_effect: OLV PPR +7-11%, book Sharpe +0.02-0.04, +$50-75k risk-matched over 16y; open OLV risk rises only in pullbacks where it is currently low (flow 19.9/yr at 3-10 vs 16.2 at < 3 but shallower stacks). PIT-clean by construction (a price state).
changes.confidence: moderate
changes.evidence: cycle_macro finding 6 and recommendation 2; finding 1 (book earns ~60% more R per unit risk in 3-10% pullbacks; sdR flat, so an edge effect); outside: Nagel 2012 liquidity-provision premium in stress
changes.intuition: OLV is liquidity provision in single names; it is paid most when the index has already pulled back and the names it buys are the selloff, not idiosyncratic decay.
changes.risks: Partly a beta channel (SPY fwd 10d +1.25% off-high vs +0.46% near-high); re-test on hedged returns if XS-1 ships before it; multiple comparisons (~900 cells) mean only mechanism + LOYO + WF cells are cited.
changes.implementation_notes: Generic market_state_bands execution field (SPY state at signal close, computed in daily_scan from the cache and in strat_backtester PIT); prereg doc; tests.

changes.name: Haircut on backtest edge: 40% central (keep 0.60), range 27-71%, per-strategy keeps in the tilt, standing 15% survivorship cut on overflow-heavy longs, commissions and MKT-exit spread added to the engine
changes.rule: Book: h = 0.40 in every frontier and growth number; sensitivity rows at 0.27 and 0.71. Strategies: keep_s per ST-1; overflow-heavy long strategies (OLV, LT Trend ST OS, St OS Sznl, 52wh overflow) carry an additional 0.85 survivorship keep until the point-in-time overflow universe lands, liquid single-stock longs 0.95, index/ETF strategies and shorts 1.0. Engine: add $0.005/share ($1 floor, both sides) and an ADV-bucketed MKT/MOC exit half-spread (1.5-12 bps); limit entries and target limits stay cost-free. Re-derive after 150 broker-matched fills and after 2027 Q1; 2026's 0.52x realized edge per unit risk is treated as the midterm base rate (0.27 avg for prior midterm Jan-Aug windows), not decay, with OLV and LT Trend flagged for the 2027 Q1 re-read.
changes.math: keep_book = 0.5 x PnL-weighted composite (0.51) + 0.5 x direct blend (0.70) = 0.605. DSR keeps 0.63-0.79 across 31-1000 trials (significance never in doubt at T > 2,700 days; it is a level correction). Costs: 5.6% of the ledger mean book-wide (OVS 8.5%, WCDS 9.7%), plus 2-4% for marginal bar-touch fills. seasonality_rules: No calendar-conditional multiplier of any kind (month, quarter, half-year, earnings season, opex week, turn-of-month, day-of-week, holiday); the 1,012-cell scan has zero FDR survivors and every fitted or unfitted calendar rule replays at or below baseline OOS (seasonality_flow). Closed.

Seasonal variance is flow, not risk: May-Oct sd 63 vs 83 bps/day comes with a proportional mean (Kelly ratio 1.03-1.06); the GRM frontier is computed on full years and no vol-target keys on seasonally low realized vol; January's excess variance is 8 episodic high-open-risk years and belongs to the dial-armed hedge (XS-1), not the calendar.

Flow is a same-day and 5-day STATE, never a month: size up (FL-2, 1.25x) and let the per-strategy cap breathe (FL-1, 375 bps) when the family's trailing-5d raw candidate count is in its top tercile (dip_buy >= 6 with dial < 50, oversold_hold >= 7, short_fade >= 104); never size down on high flow (wrong-signed in every mean-reverting family); no flow rule for breakouts.

Signal quality inside a strategy is sized by expectancy, never win rate: OVS bottom-extremity (mean short-window rank < 94) at 0.5x (ST-3); adds graded up with depth in OLV / WCDS / LT Trend (AD-2, AD-3); 52wh >= 6 open at 0.5x as tail insurance only (AD-4).

Earnings handling stays per-name (OVS +/-10 td blackout, OLV and St OS Sznl per-name overrides), never per-season: in-season trades that pass the blackouts run avgR 0.52-0.64 vs 0.41-0.48 off-season in 14 of 15 strategies, so a season haircut is wrong-signed (-7.1% PnL, 0-1 of 24 years better).

Presidential cycle: keep OVS cycle_risk_mults {2: 0.75} (6 of 6 midterm years below, year-clustered t -2.00); no book-wide midterm cut (Sharpe-neutral, risk-matched maxDD 0.5 pt worse); read 2026's 0.52x realized edge as the midterm base rate (prior midterm Jan-Aug windows averaged 0.27x) with OLV and LT Trend on a 2027 Q1 re-read.

The only seasonal items in the risk architecture are operational: the hedge's quarterly ES/MES roll on the panel's roll-off schedule, the 15:45 ET Soft-Edge-Margin clock every day, and the OVS Friday-only EOD-DD already in place; September's post-opex cell is already the event sleeve's T3 and must not be double-counted.

Watch items with written triggers, no rules: dip-buy family May-Oct gap (re-open as a 0.75x September-only appetite decision only if the gap stays below -0.15 and the September dip-buy cell is <= 0 after 20 more fills, ~2029); OLV post-print 0.5x at +20 trades; OVS same-day-cluster 1.25x pre-registered behind FL-1.
what_not_to_do: No book-level scalar throttle, vol target, dial taper, open-leg 1/sqrt(n), VIX-inverse or EWMA overlay: nine overlays at or below baseline at equal vol (plan section 4), PIT throttle t -0.23, taper -11.4R; outside, Cederburg 2020 / Barroso-Detzel 2021 say real-time vol management fails for everything but momentum, and the book's ATR sizing already is the asset-level vol target.

No VIX-armed, VIX-percentile-armed, drawdown-armed or always-on beta hedge: -$158.5k (0 of 15 episodes positive, t -3.85), -$154k (3/21), -$139k (2/14), -$478k always-hedged with maxDD -8.3 -> -11.5%; the book's beta is 0.17 and its Sharpe 3.8 when VIX > 30. The dial is the only arming variable with a negative conditional SPY drift.

No drawdown-triggered cut of any form (pod-shop 50% at -5% / stop at -7.5%, Grossman-Zhou continuous de-lever, cut-until-new-high): book PnL is negatively autocorrelated (acf1 -0.035, acf2 -0.055, VR21 0.86, LB p 0.008 on 2010+), the next day after 3 down days averages 27.5 bps vs 11.2 base, drawdown state has no forward content (dd > 5%: fwd21 2.26% vs 2.34%), and the replays cost Sharpe (pod rule 2.25 -> 2.14 with equal-vol maxDD -12.1 -> -14.1%; GZ 0.9: 2.25 -> 2.23 for maxDD -11.3%). Kaminski-Lo: negative stopping premium on mean-reverting PnL. The GM-3 floor at -25% is a ruin control, not a cut.

No correlation-spike, effective-N or signal-cluster de-risking: rolling effective N is uncorrelated with the dial (Spearman -0.02) and VIX (+0.05); the worst 5% of book days have theme correlation -0.13 and effective N 17 (single-theme events), and the high-correlation cluster days (5-6 strategies active, beta 1.13) have Sharpe 4.7. Correlation is handled at L3 by the hedge and at L2 by the tail formula, nowhere else.

No per-leg Kelly-concurrency (1 + n rho), variance-parity, sqrt-n, sector, same-ticker, trailing-63d-correlation or stack-age cut in OLV, OVS, WCDS, LT Trend or the 3x fades: adds are the higher-edge legs everywhere but 52wh >= 6, and every such cut loses PnL per unit risk (OLV 0.651/0.678 vs 0.790; rho > 0.6 cuts lose in five strategies; same-ticker 0.5x on OLV 0.715). No OLV sleeve open-risk cap at 250-400 bps (-$70k/16y for -$3.4k worst-21d); the AD-1 bound sits past the p99 by design.

No notional-denominated sizing caps (McKinley's standing rule); the margin-feasibility guard (GM-4) is a broker constraint on staged entries, never a size rule, and the retired 100%-NAV OLV book cap stays retired.
No switch of the sizing base to live NAV while NLV < $750k (a 16% risk cut, not a growth step) and no full compounding until the measured haircut is under 25%; no upward rebase inside a quarter.

No calendar multipliers of any kind, and no revival of the retired cells (Sep 0.5x, Aug-Sep 0.75x, May-Oct 0.75x, Nov-Apr 1.25x, Dec/Q4 1.25x, opex dip-buy cut, TOM tilts, holiday tilts, OLV Aug cut, LT Trend Jun cut, 52wh Oct boost, OVS Dec boost, Jan de-rate, Fri de-rate) without a new mechanism and a single pre-registered cell.

No earnings-season haircut beyond the existing per-name blackouts/overrides (wrong-signed: in-season better in 7 of 7 single-stock strategies, LOYO all positive); no book-wide midterm cut ex-OVS; no rates/credit/term-structure/trend-state/P-C-fear scalar at the book level (all Sharpe-flat or negative walk-forward; SPY-below-200d and negative-momentum tape are LOWER variance with higher Sharpe).

No within-strategy tier on the current-weights dial, VIX, P/C fear, ATR%, 200-SMA distance, universe tier or book-wide signal density (the OLV dial gradient t -3.24 becomes t +0.03 on PIT; 46 monotone |t| >= 2 hits against 27 expected by chance); and never a P(win)-based selectivity layer (win rate and expectancy are decoupled by design; the deleted ML meta-labeller's SKIP bucket averaged +0.60R).

No full removal of the per-strategy 250 bps cap on high-flow days (x99: short_fade Sharpe 1.18 -> 0.93, maxDD -$44k -> -$127k) and no scaling of the cap with GRM below 3.0; no 0.5x/1.5x flow multipliers (worse than 0.75/1.25 in every family); no down-side 0.75x flow leg (costs 5.7% PnL).

No NQ or IWM/RTY as the hedge instrument (QQQ lowest R2 in every regime; IWM's extra PnL is the small-cap factor's -31.9% armed-day drift, not fit, and it worsens hedged maxDD), no hedge ratio above 1.0x (Sharpe falls, maxDD -10.2% at 2x), no 42d/63d beta as the hedge ratio (zero predictive correlation when armed), no FAMILY4 + OLV sub-book target (a third to two thirds of the whole-book hedge), no 65/60 threshold as primary (t 0.99 on PIT, a Feb-2020 result).

No stacking rules on the 3x fades (every cell is 1-3 episodes); no 52wh 0.5x at >= 5 open (cuts a 1.71R cell, -$9.4k at equal risk); no doubling of OVS P2 base bps (0.280 vs 0.298, only the aggregate cap moves); no OLV cut on the SPY-near-highs side (-$18k risk-matched, cell still +0.56R).

No sizing of pilots off their own point estimates (Monthly Weak Close per-trade SR 3.5 at N 14; 3x Leader Gap Fade N 24) and no proportional scale-up of the overflow tier with GRM: overflow longs carry survivorship (upper-bound avgR), 2x the impact cost of liquid names, and the ADV participation cap binds there at roughly current size; route any size increase to the liquid tier and index legs.
narrative:
## What the book is, seen as a risk portfolio

Aggregate the fifteen strategies into the six themes that actually share a mechanism (dip_buy_index, dip_buy_stock, oversold_hold, short_fade, bear_etf_fade, breakout) and the book is a six-asset portfolio with pairwise correlation 0.06, effective N 4.4-4.7, Sharpe 2.25 (2010+) / 2.77 (2016-07+) before any haircut, and a tail that is NOT a correlation phenomenon: on its worst 5% of days the average theme correlation is -0.13 and the effective N is 17. The book's bad days are one theme on its own worst day (2015-03-25 dip_buy_stock, 2021-01-27 short_fade, 2014-01-24 breakout, 2019-10-01 dip_buy_stock). Breakout is the theme whose tail exceeds its share (37% of worst-5%-day loss for 18% of PnL, highest variance elasticity). The one state where correlation genuinely rises is the dial's top bucket (65+: effective N 3.3, SPY-explained variance 31%, book beta 0.41, SPY drift -24% ann on the live vintage / -8% on PIT), and there the factor lives in oversold_hold (43% of SPY covariance) and breakout (31%), not in the dip-buy family the fragility bands already cut. Everything in this plan follows from those three facts: budget by theme, bound each theme's one-day tail, hedge the factor when the dial says its drift has turned, and let growth theory set the total.

## The number: GRM 2.25 in two steps, without a drawdown constraint

The growth curve g(m) = E[log(1 + m r)] is linear to within a point through m = 3 on every window and haircut (risk_arch_04, unconstrained_growth), so curvature says nothing about the multiplier. At the measured 40% haircut (estimation_haircut: keep 0.60, range 27-71%) the book at GRM 1.5 is 7.7% of Kelly; the practitioner floor in the literature is 25% of honest Kelly. Growth at h = 0.40 goes 21.9% -> 30.4% -> 39.7% (2016-07+) and 13.4% -> 19.5% -> 25.4% (2003+) across m = 1 / 1.5 / 2, with 1y median drawdown 6.7% -> 9.9% -> 13.1%, P(1y DD > 20%) 0 -> 2 -> 10% (2016+) or 0 -> 5 -> 19% (2003+), and historical-path drawdowns of -11 / -16 / -21% (2016+) and -16 / -25 / -33% (2003+). Those are the drawdowns accepted at each step; they are disclosed, not constrained. What actually stops the number is two step functions. First, portfolio margin: because the sizing unit is ATR risk with no notional dimension, low-ATR index ETFs bought in size produce a max historical requirement of 55% of the base at plain PM rates (my class map; 63% on the growth study's finer map), so feasibility on the max day is m 1.6-1.8 on the base and 1.3-1.5 on the live $632k NLV, with concentration or rules-based 3x rates pulling it to 1.0-1.15. Those max days are long dip-buy clusters that carry half the book's PnL, so the answer is a margin-feasibility guard on NEW entries (GM-4) plus moving the index legs to futures (GM-5), after which the p99 day governs and margin allows m 2.2-3.0. Second, the flat $750k base on a $632k account already runs 1.19x its intended fraction, so GRM 2.25 is 1.78x in NAV terms and sits exactly on the plain-PM max-day wall on live NLV. Hence GRM 2.0 now (inside every wall on the p99 day and inside the max-day wall on the base), 2.25 once the guard and the hedge are live and IBKR's what-if margin has been queried on the four historical peak books, and 2.5-3.0 only after the index legs migrate and the haircut is measured at or under 40% on 150 matched fills. The per-strategy 250 bps cap stays fixed in effective bps through 2.25 (cost ~1 pt of growth, binds 2% of strategy-days) because it alone bounds the day that was the entire uncapped maxDD; it breathes only with flow state (FL-1), never with GRM.

## Sizing base and sequencing

Keep the flat $750k base while NLV is between 75% and 100% of it; above, half-compounding quarterly, never below the prior quarter (10y median terminal 9x vs 4.3x flat vs 25.6x full compounding at unchanged %-of-peak drawdown, dollar drawdowns growing at half the full-compounding rate; P(compounding < flat) 9-24% at 3y in the haircut cells, ~0% at 10y). Below 75% the base steps down with NLV so the constant-dollar book, which is a martingale on a shrinking account, hands over to constant-fraction before the account is also the margin. That floor fires only past the worst historical-path drawdown at GRM 2.25 and is a ruin control, not a drawdown cut: the book's PnL is negatively autocorrelated (acf1 -0.035, acf2 -0.055, VR21 0.86), the next day after three down days averages 2.5x the base, and every drawdown-cut replay (pod template, Grossman-Zhou) costs Sharpe at equal vol, so cutting on drawdown is closed here as it is in Kaminski-Lo.

## Allocation: themes, then strategies, then adds

Theme budgets (TH-1) come from a shrunk Sigma^-1 mu on the six theme series, half-blended and clipped [0.75, 1.25]: breakout 0.85, dip_buy_index 1.10, oversold_hold 1.10, the rest 1.0; both the 2010+ and 2016-07+ windows agree on the breakout cut (variance share 27% vs a Kelly-implied 13.5%) and the dip-buy-index / oversold-hold raises. Inside each theme the plan's capped half-tilt on strategies (ST-1) stands, with the per-strategy keep factors (3x fades and index dip-buys ~0.7-0.8; OLV 0.45-0.60; WCDS 0.37; 52wh 0.31-0.50; OVS held at 1.0 because its caps, not its base bps, bind) as the mu shrinkage instead of a flat 50%; pilots capped at half their ledger mean and stepped up on trade count (ST-2). Within strategies, the only quality tier that clears every bar is OVS's bottom extremity (ST-3, 0.5x below mean rank 94: +12.9% R per unit risk, LOYO 80%), and the OVS P2 aggregate cap doubles (ST-4) because it trims the best mild-gap days for a -$1.4k worst extra day.

Adds are sized by marginal expected R because that is what the evidence supports everywhere but 52wh at six or more open: the n-th leg of an OLV / OVS / WCDS / LT Trend stack is the better leg, same-sector and same-ticker adds are better still, ex-ante correlation with open names predicts nothing, and every variance-lens rule (Kelly concurrency, sqrt-n, rho cuts, 250-400 bps sleeve caps) loses PnL per unit risk. So the OLV ladder is re-keyed to max(recency rung, depth rung) (AD-2), WCDS and LT Trend go solo 0.75 / adds 1.25 (AD-3, better PnL/risk AND lower maxDD), 52wh gets 0.5x at six open as tail insurance (AD-4), clones are clamped where they carry no extra edge (IOB SPY+QQQ, cross-strategy same-ticker dip-buy pairs) and left alone where they do (MonFri). The budget on all of this is a tail formula, not a variance tax (AD-1): open ATR risk per theme times the theme's realized stress multiple k (worst-day loss per unit of open risk: p99.9 of 1.5 for oversold_hold, 2.4-2.75 for the dip-buys and short_fade, 1.28 for the book) may not exceed 8% of the base per theme or 15% for the book at the current GRM. That bound sits past the p99 of every theme's open-risk distribution, so it touches roughly five OLV legs in 21 years (the 22-leg January-2025 stack) and none of the plan's rejected 250-400 bps caps are re-created. Flow is the one state variable adopted (FL-1 cap relief to 375 bps on the family's top-tercile 5d flow days, tails byte-identical; FL-2 up-only 1.25x, 17 of 17 years better, Sharpe-flat by construction), because for the mean-reverting families signal density is the edge, and the crowded-selloff reading is wrong-signed.

## The dial: hedge the factor, do not cut the book

The dial moves composition and factor exposure, not variance, so its control belongs at the factor: a dial-armed whole-book beta hedge in ES/MES (XS-1) at threshold 50/45 with a 126d shrunk beta and 1.0x ratio, which passes the pre-registered PIT ship rule (13 episodes, 10 positive, clustered t 1.68, bootstrap P(<= 0) 0.046, placebo rank 1.000) and in my replay lifts Sharpe 2.90 -> 3.07 and improves the worst 21-day window from -6.3% to -5.2% of NAV on PIT (2.78 -> 2.85 and the same worst-21d gain on the live vintage). Its role in the frontier is modest (historical-path DD -15.9% -> -14.3% at GRM 2.25); its role in the architecture is that it acts on the one thing the dial forecasts while keeping the book's convexity (beta_up 0.79 vs beta_down 0.26 at 65+) that a cut destroys. The target is the whole book (the factor sits in oversold_hold and breakout at high dial, not in FAMILY4 + OLV), the instrument is SPY futures (never NQ, never IWM), and the VIX-gated variant is pre-registered as a second stage. Every VIX-, drawdown- or vol-armed version is dead (the book's beta is highest in calm tape at the highs and lowest after vol arrives). The fragility bands and P/C tables stay as shipped; the 0.25x/zero cell is to be re-scored on hedged returns once the hedge is live (RG-1); the plan's P2 re-test runs at the 50 line on PIT, where LT Trend ST OS is the one exemption that fails (RG-2) and OLV / OVS are confirmed exempt; OLV's 1.25x in 3-10% SPY pullbacks is the one price-state tilt worth pre-registering (RG-3). The momentum factor (15% of book variance at high dial, carried by OLV / 52wh / LTT / 3x Fade) is the exposure the SPY hedge does not touch and goes on the panel (XS-3, MS-1).

## Seasonality, quality and variance

No calendar layer of any kind: zero of 1,012 cells survive year-clustered FDR, every fitted calendar multiplier is at or below baseline out of sample, and every outside prior replays negative on this book. Seasonal variance is flow (summer vol 0.76x with mean 0.61x, Kelly ratio 1.03), so nothing vol-targets on it. Flow is used as a same-day / 5-day state, never as a month; quality is used where it is expectancy (OVS extremity, add depth), never win rate; earnings and the presidential cycle stay per-name and per-strategy as they are. Watch items carry written triggers.

## Haircut and measurement

Every number above is sized at h = 0.40 with 0.27 and 0.71 as the range, per-strategy keeps in the tilt, an additional 0.85 on overflow-heavy longs for survivorship, commissions and market-exit spread added to the engine (the ledger is ~6% optimistic), pilots capped at half their mean. There is no true out-of-sample record (108 post-freeze trades), the 2026 realized edge per unit risk is 0.52x the ledger and matches the midterm base rate, and no dial-conditioned claim is trusted on the current-weights vintage (the OLV dial gradient goes from t -3.24 to t +0.03 on PIT). The plan therefore ships with its own measurement: broker-fill reconciliation from the DO ring, PIT scoring for every dial test, an engine replay gate on every sizing change, and a hedge-panel risk block that shows gross/NAV, blended margin rate, the -30% scenario, theme open risk against its ceiling, stack n_eff, the stress multiple, effective N and the momentum loading. The staged GRM path is the disclosure of what the walls are and the order in which they get moved.

lens: practitioner (discretionary-quant PM: market intuition, seasonality, flow, liquidity, execution reality, broker constraints)
thesis: The book is not drawdown-limited, it is broker-limited and composition-limited. Growth theory says it runs at 6-13% of Kelly and the growth curve is linear through 3x current size; the haircut work says the honest edge is about 60% of the ledger; the outside base rates say 25-50% of honest Kelly is where careful practitioners live, which is 2-4x today's size. None of that is what stops you. What stops you is (a) the historical peak margin-requirement day (dip-buy index clusters like 2016-06-14, 2013-11-04: gross 4.4x NAV at CURRENT size, requirement 61% of the $750k base at stylised PM rates and 72% of the live ~$632k NLV) and (b) the fact that every evidenced overlay in this study is an UP-size on the same legs on the same days: when I stack the tilt, the OLV depth ladder, the OLV pullback tilt and the flow boost as separate analysts proposed them, the 2016+ maxDD moves from -7.3% to -11.7% and the new worst episode is Jun-Jul 2026 OLV, an episode the current book barely noticed. So the plan is: press through the evidenced growth levers (flow, cluster adds, OVS cluster cap, tilt toward the diversifiers), but with three practitioner constraints the single-overlay studies could not see: a per-strategy composition clip (OLV product capped at 1.5x pre-GRM, OLV tilt 1.15 not 1.29), a margin-headroom guard that switches the up-size layers off exactly on the peak-gross days, and non-stacking of the cap reliefs. That package (my replay 'package_C', 2010-2026, cap re-applied) at today's GRM is +12% PnL, Sharpe 2.20 to 2.38, maxDD -12.4% to -10.0%, worst 21d -9.5% to -6.4%, 17 of 22 years better; at GRM 1.875 it is +35% PnL versus today with the SAME maxDD as today's book (-12.5% vs -12.4%), worst day -7.3%, and a peak requirement of 71% of the base. GRM 1.875 now; 2.25 only after the guard is live, the index-ETF dip-buy legs are routed to micro futures, and IBKR's what-if confirms the three peak-gross books. Nothing keys on the calendar; the calendar is dead in this book. Drawdowns are accepted as an output, not set as an input; the one thing I will not accept is a forced liquidation at 15:45 on the book's best day.

grm.value: 1.875 now (m = 1.25x current), with a written step to 2.25 (m = 1.5x) gated on three deliverables: the order_staging margin-headroom guard (GM-2) live, the index-ETF dip-buy legs routed through MES/MNQ/MYM/M2K (GM-3), and an IBKR what-if margin run on the 2013-11-04, 2016-06-14 and 2023-02-03 books scaled to the target. Re-derive quarterly and whenever live NLV moves 20%. Applied together with the package in the changes list; the number is chosen for the PACKAGE, not for the current book.
grm.rationale: Growth side: g(m) is linear to within 1 pt through m=3 on every window and haircut (unconstrained_growth_01: g(1)=21.9%/32.7% for 2003+/2016+, g(1.5)=32.3%/48.4%, g(2)=42.5%/63.7%); at a 50% haircut the growth optimum is still m 9-12; fractional-Kelly base rates (Thorp/Benter/Ziemba 1/4 to 1/2 of honest Kelly; Carver half-Sharpe-then-half-Kelly = ~25% of backtest Kelly) put the defensible band at 2-4x current. The haircut study's central keep of 0.60 (range 0.29-0.73) makes honest Sharpe ~1.2-1.3 on the 2016+ series, so m=1.25 is ~10% of honest Kelly, still under every practitioner floor. Boundary side, which is what actually binds: on the historical peak-requirement day the stylised PM requirement is 61% of the $750k base at m=1 (unconstrained_growth_02: binds at m 1.60 on the max day, 2.46 on the p99 day, 1.34 on live NLV ~$632k); my package replay at GRM 1.875 with reliefs non-stacked and headroom-guarded shows a peak requirement of 71% of the base (84% of live NLV), which survives a 35% IBKR house uplift on the base (0.96) but not on live NLV (1.14): that is exactly the margin of safety a desk wants before going further, and it is why 2.25 (peak 84% of base, 100% of live NLV) waits for GM-2/GM-3. Live NLV is below the $750k constant, so flat-basis GRM 1.875 is ~2.2x of NAV-basis risk in live terms; the step is bigger than it looks and one step at a time is the practitioner rule. The per-strategy 250 bps cap stays fixed (costs ~1 pt of growth at m=1.25, binds ~3% of strategy-days) because it alone bounds the worst single day.
grm.drawdown_accepted: Stated as an output of the package at GRM 1.875, flat $750k basis. Historical replay 2010-2026 (package C, cap fixed): maxDD -12.5% (today's book: -12.4%), worst day -7.3% (today -5.9%), worst 21d -8.0% (today -9.5%), worst 63d and CVaR5 -176 bps/day (today -154); 2016-07+ maxDD -9.4%, -8.7% with the dial hedge. Stationary block bootstrap (mean block 10, 3,000 one-year paths on the 2010+ package series): no haircut median 1y maxDD 6.9%, p95 12.1%, P(>15%) 1%, P(>20%) 0%; 25% haircut median 8.1%, p95 14.1%, P(>15%) 4%, P(>20%) 0.3%; 50% haircut median 9.2%, p95 17.6%, P(>15%) 10%, P(>20%) 2.4%, P(>25%) 0.4%. At the gated 2.25 step the same table reads median 8.3/9.7/11.1%, p95 14.5/16.9/21.1%, P(>20%) 0.5/1.9/6.3% and the historical replay maxDD -15.0%, worst day -8.8%. iid base rate check (outside evidence): at Sharpe ~2 and ~15% vol the 23-year expected worst drawdown is ~1.4x annual vol (~21%), p90 ~1.8x (~27%); the overlapping-hold autocorrelation the book carries fattens that, so a 20-25% peak-to-trough year is inside the plan's expectation and is NOT a reason to cut. What is not accepted: a requirement above live NLV on any historical day, and a stack of reliefs that lands on the same day as the peak gross.

changes.name: GLOBAL_RISK_MULTIPLIER 1.5 -> 1.875, with a gated step to 2.25

The 250 bps per-strategy cap does NOT scale with GRM below 3.0.

At 2.25: 84% / 100% / 1.13 / 1.35, which fails (ii)-(iii) until GM-2/GM-3.

The 2.25 step adds a further ~+$50k/yr for maxDD -15.0% and worst day -8.8% once the boundary controls exist.
changes.confidence: moderate-high on the growth and drawdown arithmetic (three windows, two haircuts, historical path and bootstrap agree); moderate on the boundary (stylised margin rates until the IBKR what-if is run)

changes.intuition: Twenty years of watching books blow up says the ruin path is never the drawdown you modelled, it is the broker closing you out on the day every dip-buy fills at once. That day is also the book's best day (gross > 100% NAV days are 15% of days and 49% of PnL). So you size to survive that day with a house-uplift cushion and you let the drawdown be whatever it is. One step at a time because live NLV is $632k, not $750k: 1.875 flat is already ~2.2x in NAV terms.

changes.implementation_notes: One constant in strategy_config; every nominal bps, OVS path bps, earnings overrides and the OVERFLOW/overlap clamps scale by it at import; caps stay in EFFECTIVE bps (250 per strategy, OVS P2 1.125% -> see S-2). Update the pitch sanity bounds separately (they are their own contract). Commit message carries the rule's three numbers. Announce to the PA clamp too (PA is Reg-T and below the PM minimum: keep its own $30k cap).

changes.name: Margin-headroom guard in order_staging (projected requirement on live NLV)
changes.rule: Before submission, project tomorrow's requirement = open book at stylised rates (15% stock / 8% broad index ETF / 45% 3x long, 90% 3x short until IBKR confirms PM treatment / per-share minimums for sub-$16.67 shorts) + every staged entry at full size, all on LIVE NLV. If projected > 70% of NLV: scale that day's NEW entries pro rata to land at 70%. If projected > 60%: switch OFF the flow up-size (F-1) and the cap relief (F-2) for the day, and do not arm the OVS 375 cap above 250 (GM-5). Log the three numbers (gross/NLV, blended rate, projected requirement/NLV) on every scan email and the hedge panel.
changes.math: Requirement/NAV at m=1: p95 25%, p99 41%, max 63% (unconstrained_growth_02). The guard binds only on the top ~1% of days (dip-buy index clusters). In the package replay the same days are where the up-size layers fire: package C with reliefs shows a peak requirement of 88-91% of base (2023-02-03 OVS cluster with stacked OVS caps) vs 60-84% with reliefs off, so the guard converts a forced liquidation into a planned haircut on ~2-3 days a year.
changes.expected_effect: Zero PnL in expectation on 99% of days; on the binding days it trims the book's best days by the amount needed to stay solvent through a 15:45 Soft Edge Margin expiry. P(requirement > equity within 3y) at m=1.5 falls from 0.1-0.4% (plain PM) / 7-10% (with a 15% cushion) toward zero by construction. Unmeasured cost: the unconstrained_growth study notes the gross > 100% days carry 49% of PnL; a 70% ceiling touches only the top decile of those.
changes.confidence: high that it is needed before any step past 1.875; the trim's cost is unmeasured (needs its own replay on the ledger's peak-gross days)
changes.evidence: unconstrained_growth_02/02b (feasibility table, joint bootstrap with ruin absorbing, concentration scenarios); practitioner_02_package_replay (req_nav_max by config: baseline 0.61 -> package C 0.88 with stacked reliefs, 0.60 without); outside: IBKR Soft Edge Margin expires 15 min before the close, no margin calls, auto-liquidation; 2020 election house uplift 35%; Jan-2021 300% short requirements
changes.intuition: IBKR does not call you, it sells you. The OVS Friday EOD-DD, the event-sleeve MOCs and any OLV MOC land inside or after the 15:45 window when the broker is already liquidating whatever it likes. The guard is the desk's version of 'know your headroom before the open'.
changes.risks: Stylised rates can under-state the real TIMS requirement on concentrated OLV stacks (30% add-on above 25% NAV in one name would already put the CURRENT book at 89% on the max day); over-stating it costs edge on the best days. Verify with the what-if before setting the 60/70 levels; treat those as first-pass numbers.
changes.implementation_notes: order_staging.py (OneDrive): new stage after the per-strategy cap, before submission; reads live NLV from the TWS account summary; class rates in a small table keyed on LEV3X_ALL + a BROAD set; per-share minimum shorts by price. Engine parity: not modelled (the engine has no NAV concept); document as live-only like the retired OLV book cap. Test file beside test_olv_book_cap.py.

changes.name: Route the broad-index dip-buy legs to micro futures
changes.rule: SPY / QQQ / DIA / IWM legs of Weak Close Decent Sznls, Monday Dip, SPY QQQ MonFri Reversion, Indices Oversold Bounce, Monthly Weak Close and the 25%-NAV exposure leg execute in MES / MNQ / MYM / M2K at the same ATR-risk size (contracts = risk / (stop_atr x ATR_index x multiplier)), with the same limit logic expressed in index points and the same time exits. ETF execution remains the fallback when the futures gateway is down.
changes.math: Broad-index ETFs are 38% of gross on the top-1% requirement days and are margined at ~8% under TIMS vs ~5-6% as futures; moving them lifts the plain-PM feasibility multiple from m 1.60 to ~2.3 (GRM ~3.5) on the historical max day (unconstrained_growth_02b). Costs: MES/MNQ round trip ~1-2 bps plus roll; no borrow, no ETF spread at the open.
changes.expected_effect: Unlocks the GRM 2.25 step without touching ATR risk; removes the largest single-ticker concentrations (SPY > 50% NAV on 89 days since 2016, XLP 122% on 2017-04-27 remains an ETF issue). Expected PnL effect near zero; the effect is on the boundary.
changes.confidence: moderate: the arithmetic is mechanical, the execution build is not trivial (trading_ibkr already has a futures gateway design and tests per memory)
changes.evidence: unconstrained_growth_02b (class shares on top requirement days, feasibility with index legs at 5-6%); IBKR TIMS +6/-8% broad index vs futures exchange margin; memory note: futures/FX are tradeable vehicles in trading_ibkr
changes.intuition: Every macro desk carries its index beta in futures for exactly this reason; the ETF wrapper is paying 8% margin for the privilege of a spread at the open.
