Ship after X-1 is live so the panel already knows how to net index futures.

changes.name: Sizing base: flat $750k until live NLV exceeds it, then half-compounding
changes.rule: base = $750k while NLV < $750k (no downward rebase). Once NLV > $750k: base = max(prior base, 0.5 x 750k + 0.5 x NLV), reset on the first session of each quarter, never below the prior quarter's base. Full compounding only if the measured live-vs-ledger haircut (M-3) is under 25%. The margin guard (GM-2) always uses live NLV, never the base.
changes.math: 10y block bootstrap at m=1 (2016+, no haircut): flat median terminal 4.3x, full compounding 25.6x (p5 14.7x), half-compounding 9.0x; %-of-peak maxDD identical (9%); dollar drawdowns scale with NAV at half the rate under half-compounding. At a 50% haircut, m=1.5, 3y: P(compounding < flat on the same path) 9-24%, with no regret in the median even after a >15% first-year drawdown (1.62 vs 1.54).
changes.expected_effect: No change today (live NLV ~$632k means a NAV rebase would CUT risk 16%); later, most of the compounding growth with dollar drawdowns growing at half the NAV rate; the quarterly reset keeps the margin feasibility multiple constant in NAV terms.
changes.confidence: moderate
changes.evidence: unconstrained_growth_04 (flat vs compounding vs half-compounding, sequencing regret); estimation_haircut (haircut still unmeasured); memory note live NLV 2026-08-18
changes.intuition: Nobody on a desk sizes off yesterday's high-water mark daily; quarterly rebases with a ratchet are how allocators do it, and it also stops the book de-levering itself as it grows (the flat book's effective m falls to 0.23-0.6 of NAV over a median 10y path).
changes.risks: A quarter that starts at a high and ends in a drawdown carries the larger base through the drawdown; accepted (that is what the ratchet is). The PA account runs its own clamp.
changes.implementation_notes: ACCOUNT_VALUE in strategy_config stays the single source; add a quarterly job (or manual rule) that updates it from the account summary under the ratchet; every consumer (scan, engines, reports, staged Risk_Amt) reads it at import.

changes.name: Per-strategy daily cap: 250 fixed, OVS 375, reliefs non-stacking
changes.rule: cap_bps(strategy, day) = 250 x max(1.5 if strategy == OVS, 1.5 if the strategy's family is in its hi-flow state (F-2), 1.0). The reliefs take the MAX, never the product (562 bps is forbidden). No relief when GM-2's projected requirement > 60% of live NLV. The cap does not scale with GRM until GRM > 3.0, at which point scaling it becomes an explicit second decision. Pooled per-direction caps stay removed.
changes.math: Cap-bound days are the best days: OVS avgR 0.62 bound vs 0.20 unbound (101 days), Weak Close 0.96 vs 0.24, 3x ETF fade 1.25 vs 0.52; strategy-days staging >= 240 bps carry risk-weighted avgR 0.84 vs 0.41 below 100 bps. OVS P1 fills at depth >= 6 book 2.5-4 bps per fill on the biggest days because the cap pro-rates over staged signals. Replay of OVS x1.5 on cluster days: OVS PnL $607k -> $699k (+15%), PnL/risk 0.298 -> 0.327, worst day -26k -> -35k (2021-01-27), worst 21d unchanged. Cap x99 on hi-flow days blows the OVS tail (Sharpe 1.18 -> 0.93, maxDD -44k -> -127k), so the relief is bounded at 1.5x. In my package replay the OVS x1.5 and the family relief STACKED to 562 bps and produced the peak requirement day (2023-02-03, 88% of base); the non-stacked rule removes that day from the tail (peak falls back to 2016-06-14 at 60-71%).
changes.expected_effect: OVS +$92k/23y raw (+$58k at equal risk); family relief +3.8% book PnL with maxDD and worst-21d byte-identical in the flow study; combined with the up-size +9.9% PnL at +6.8% risk. Worst single OVS day widens ~35% (-$35k at GRM 1.5 basis).
changes.confidence: moderate-high on the OVS cell (episode t 2.6-4.6, LOYO floors 1.9-4.4, 8/10 years); moderate on the magnitude (a real cap change scales staged-but-unfilled rows and interacts with the P2 aggregate cap)
changes.evidence: within_strategy_adds (OVS depth cells, x1.5 / x2 replays); flow_conditional (cap x1.5 on hi-flow days: book +3.8%, tails identical; x99 negative); signal_quality (cap-bound strategy-days 0.84R); practitioner_02 (stacked-relief peak day); CLAUDE.md Daily Risk Caps (2026-07-10/16 studies: the 250 cap alone bounds the worst day -$44k vs -$118k)
changes.intuition: The cap is the one throttle that pays for itself because it bounds the 2021-01-27 short-squeeze kind of day; the cluster days are where OVS earns, so give them room but not unlimited room, and never let two reliefs multiply on the same day.
changes.risks: Order_staging's placed totals vs the ledger's implied ones are unverified; the 2021-01-27 tail is exactly the day the cap exists for and it gets 35% worse; P2 cap interaction not replayed.
changes.implementation_notes: Aligned: order_staging PER_STRAT_DAILY_CAP_DOLLARS['Overbot Vol Spike'] = 375 bps x base, a per-day family-flow flag the scanner stamps (see F-1), engine process_signals_fast cap_bps per strategy-day (cap x strat mult hook exists), build_trade_ledger, strat_backtester UI default, tests/test_pooled_cap_sequential.py sibling. Guard the non-stacking with a test.

changes.name: No drawdown-, streak- or vol-triggered book cut; hold size through a hit
changes.rule: No sizing rule may key on the book's trailing P&L, drawdown from high, losing streak, realized book vol or VIX. After a worst-5% book day the next session's staged size is unchanged (the flow rule may raise it; nothing lowers it). Codify beside the book-wide throttle in CLAUDE.md with the ACF numbers.
changes.math: NEW evidence this session (practitioner_01): flat-basis daily book P&L ACF at lags 1-2 is NEGATIVE (2003+: -0.031 / -0.062; 2016+: -0.057 / -0.055; 2se 0.026 / 0.039), Ljung-Box p < 0.001 (10 lags) and variance ratios 0.82-0.88 at 5-21 days, i.e. the P&L series mean-reverts. Kaminski-Lo (2014): the stopping premium of a cut is negative under a random walk and negative to first order under mean reversion. Conditional forward returns: after a worst-5% day the next 5 sessions average +135 bps vs +40 (blocked t +2.8; 2016+: +190 vs +62, t +2.4) and the next 21 sessions +295 vs +183 bps; drawdown states (5-10% off the 252d high, n=431) forecast nothing (fwd21 +185 vs +189, t -0.07); 5+ down-day streaks forecast nothing (t -0.07). |r| ACF 0.35 at lag 1 is vol clustering from open positions, the flow phenomenon, not a sizing signal.
changes.expected_effect: Zero PnL versus current; avoids the -2.2%/yr class of cost measured for mechanical drawdown cut-offs on good strategies (Man 2025) and the Grossman-Zhou growth tax (1 - alpha). Every scalar overlay the baseline tested (nine) sits at or below baseline at equal vol; every VIX-armed control in the cross-strategy study lost (-$139k to -$158k, 0-3 of 14-21 episodes positive).
changes.confidence: high
changes.evidence: practitioner_01_acf_drawdown.json (new); dynamic_sizing_plan section 4 (nine overlays); cross_strategy_regime (VIX/drawdown arming dead); cycle_macro (vol-direct daily overlays within +-0.03 Sharpe, 5-7 of 11 years on 2016+); outside: Kaminski-Lo 2014, Cederburg et al 2020, Man Group 2025, Van Hemert et al 2020
changes.intuition: Dip-buy books lose in violent clusters and earn the recovery; cutting after the cluster sells the recovery. The pod-shop 5%/7.5% template solves the allocator's information problem, not the operator's, and you have the signal-level evidence they do not.
changes.risks: A genuinely broken strategy shows up as a drawdown too; the answer is per-strategy retirement triggers on multi-year evidence (S-1's two-consecutive-years rule), not a size throttle after a bad month.
changes.implementation_notes: Documentation only plus a negative-registry entry; add the ACF table to the risk tab's display block (X-4).

changes.name: Headroom and factor display on the hedge panel (display only)
changes.rule: Add to the Exec tab hedge panel, daily: gross/NLV and gross/base, blended stylised TIMS rate, projected requirement/NLV, implied loss under a -30% one-day equity scenario as a fraction of NLV (the IBKR exposure-fee screen), rolling 126d book beta with the up-day / down-day split, effective N (126d) and number of active strategies, the book's 12-1 momentum-factor loading, per-strategy share of SPY covariance while the hedge is armed, OLV stack n_eff, and the current regime row (VIX, rv21, SPY drawdown state, cycle year) with the book's historical PnL/risk and open risk in that state. None of it sizes anything.
changes.math: n/a (display). Reference numbers to show: book beta 0.21 at dial < 30 vs 0.41 at 65+, R2 10% vs 31%; momentum loading ~15% of book variance at dial >= 50 carried by OLV / 52wh / LTT / 3x fade; open risk 204 bps mean in rv21 < 12 tape vs 51 at rv21 30+.
changes.expected_effect: Makes the size of the single market bet, the un-hedged momentum-crash exposure and the distance to the broker's two step functions (liquidation, exposure fee) visible before the day's orders go out.
changes.confidence: high (display)
changes.evidence: cross_strategy_regime (findings 1, 4, 6, 7); cycle_macro (finding 2: inventory inverted vs edge); unconstrained_growth_02; outside: IBKR exposure fee (1-day -30% scenario), TIMS class rates
changes.intuition: You cannot manage what the panel does not show; the August 2026 manual hedge was sized by feel because the beta and the stack size were not on the screen.
changes.risks: None on PnL; risk of false precision on the stylised margin numbers until the what-if calibrates them.
changes.implementation_notes: site/assets/execution.js hedge panel + scripts/build_betas.py extension (up/down betas, 126d), build_risk_json regime block; reads /exec-book, betas.json, rd2_fragility, strategy_daily.

changes.name: Replace the 50% placeholder haircut with 40% central (27-71 range) and per-strategy keep factors
changes.rule: Book mu haircut = 40% (keep 0.60) for every L4 frontier row, with 27% and 71% as the sensitivity rows. Per-strategy keep_s as the mu shrinkage inside the L1 tilt: 3x ETF Fade 0.78, 3x Bear 0.74, ATR Ext 0.73, MonFri 0.72, Monday Dip 0.69, IOB 0.68, Sector BO 0.65, St OS 0.50, OLV 0.45 (judgement 0.45-0.60), 3x Leader 0.44, Monthly WC 0.44, LT Trend 0.41, WCDS 0.37, 52wh 0.31 (judgement 0.35-0.50), OVS 0.30 (judgement 0.40-0.55). Pilots with N < 50: mean capped at 0.5x the ledger value. Long single-stock overflow-heavy strategies carry a standing 0.85 survivorship keep, liquid long single-stock 0.95, index/ETF and shorts 1.0. Re-derive after 150 broker-matched fills and after 2027 Q1.
changes.math: keep_book = 0.5 x PnL-weighted composite (0.51) + 0.5 x direct blend (0.70) = 0.605. Components: deflated-Sharpe selection keep 0.63-0.79 across a 30x trial-count range (E[max SR] over 23y is only 0.33-0.68 for N=10-1000, so the book-level selection haircut is bounded); realized 2026 risk-weighted ratio 0.52 (midterm-conditioned ~1.0, average 0.76); cost keep 0.92; survivorship 0.95 book-level. Outside base rates bracket it: McLean-Pontiff -26% OOS / -58% post-pub, Ilmanen -30%, Falck-Rej-Thesmar -43%, Suhonen -73% median (sell-side products), Chen-Velikov ~0 net for textbook anomalies.
changes.expected_effect: Turns the L4 frontier into a measured statement; the frontier at 40% sits between the plan's 'none' and '50%' rows; per-strategy keeps move the tilt toward MonFri, IOB, the 3x fades, ATR Ext and Monday Dip and away from WCDS, 52wh, LT Trend, St OS Sznl and the pilots (see S-1).
changes.confidence: moderate: both estimators bracket 0.60 and neither is independent of the 2026 year
changes.evidence: estimation_haircut_06 (DSR grid), 05b/05c (2026 realized, midterm conditioning), 04 (survivorship), 08 (costs), 09 (synthesis); outside evidence packs on backtest-to-live decay
changes.intuition: The book's edges are old, simple and conditional (index dip-buys, vol-spike fades), which is the population that decays least; the 2026-vintage overlays and the overflow longs are the population that decays most. One number for the book, a different one per strategy.
changes.risks: The 108-trade post-freeze OOS window is uninformative (CI on the ratio spans -0.57 to 1.22); 2026 is one partial midterm year; the trial-count judgement (versions/3) moves per-strategy keeps by 0.1-0.2.
changes.implementation_notes: scratch/pit-style frontier script reads keep_book; the L1 tilt script multiplies mu by keep_s before the shrunk Sigma^-1 mu solve; a committed JSON of keeps with the date and N behind each.

changes.name: Engine cost model: commissions and MKT/MOC exit spread
changes.rule: process_signals_fast charges $0.005/share with a $1 minimum on both sides, plus an ADV-bucketed half-spread on every MKT / MOC / stop exit (1.5 bps > $100M ADV, 3 bps $25-100M, 6 bps $5-25M, 12 bps below). Limit entries and target limits stay cost-free (they earn the spread per Nagel's 0.30 vs 0.18 %/day decomposition).
changes.math: Book cost 0.025 R/trade = 5.6% of avgR 0.453 (liquid 4.3%, overflow 6.6%); WCDS 9.7%, OVS 8.5% (the $1 floor on small scale-out tranches), LT Trend 6.3%; bar-touch marginal fills add a further 1.8-3.8%. Ledger avgR 0.453 -> ~0.428.
changes.expected_effect: Removes ~6% systematic optimism from every ledger number the tilt and the frontier read; no live behaviour change.
changes.confidence: high
changes.evidence: estimation_haircut_08; broker journal Feb-2026 ($0.005/share, 0 bps limit slippage); outside: Frazzini-Israel-Moskowitz 12-20 bps live institutional costs, Novy-Marx-Velikov 20-57 bps per trade for mid-turnover anomalies
changes.intuition: Every desk backtest I have seen that ignored the $1 minimum on odd lots over-stated a scale-out strategy; OVS's near tranches are exactly that.
changes.risks: MOC auction prints likely cost less than the proxy, overflow opens more; the overflow ADV proxy is coarse.
changes.implementation_notes: pages/strat_backtester.py process_signals_fast (kwargs with prod defaults), build_trade_ledger rebuild, site payloads re-derive; guard test with a known trade.

changes.name: Live-vs-ledger reconciliation from broker fills, and the IBKR margin what-if
changes.rule: Schedule trade_journal.py (OneDrive) daily and harvest the DO fills ring (14-day retention) so no fill is lost; match on orderRef (SYMBOL|ACTION|Strategy|Date) to ledger trade keys; publish live R / ledger R and the staged-limit fill rate on the Execution tab. Separately, run IBKR's what-if margin on the 2013-11-04, 2016-06-14 and 2023-02-03 books scaled to GRM 1.875 and 2.25, and read the Exposure Fee Calculation Report at current, 1.5x and 2x gross via Risk Navigator custom scenarios. Until >= 150 matched fills exist, live R = ledger R is the working assumption and Fill_Status in Trade_Signals_Log is not cited as live evidence (it is yfinance-modelled).
changes.math: n/a. What exists: 882 staged rows 2026-03-26 to 08-31, 121 matched ledger trades at avgR 0.197, fill-decision parity 100% on expired / 69% on filled with every gap explained; broker journal 27 rows.
changes.expected_effect: Turns the execution component of the haircut from assumed (~0) to measured, and replaces the stylised margin rates with the broker's own before the 2.25 step.
changes.confidence: high that it is needed; unknown what it shows
changes.evidence: estimation_haircut_07; unconstrained_growth_02 caveats; IBKR documentation (what-if, exposure fee report)
changes.intuition: Nobody steps up size on a desk without the prime broker's margin sheet for the worst historical day in hand.
changes.risks: None; cost is a few hours.

changes.name: Capped half-tilt on base bps, with practitioner overrides on the two raises the 2026 tape argues with
changes.rule: Multiplier per strategy = clip(0.5 w + 0.5, 0.6, 1.4), w the expanding-window shrunk Sigma^-1 mu weight through the prior December with mu shrunk by keep_s (M-1), re-fit each January, engine confirmation P3 before go-live. Shipping set from the 2025 fit with overrides: 52wh 0.73, IOB 0.83, Sector BO 0.84, WCDS 0.84, St OS Sznl 0.92, Monday Dip 1.02, ATR Ext 1.04, 3x ETF Fade 1.15, MonFri 1.16, LT Trend ST OS 1.10 (mechanical 1.19), OLV 1.15 (mechanical 1.29); OVS, 3x Bear, 3x Leader, Monthly WC 1.0. Retirement trigger: expanding weight below 0.6 two Januaries running.
changes.math: Walk-forward 2014-2026, vol-matched: half-blend expanding PnL 24.2 -> 28.2% NAV/yr, Sharpe 2.05 -> 2.15, PnL/maxDD +18%, 12 of 13 years better, worst held-out year -13%; both routes (per-trade exact Kelly with concurrency, daily Sigma^-1 mu) agree on the four cuts. Tail ownership: the four cut strategies own 61% of worst-5%-day losses for 36% of PnL; the raises own 12% for 25%. Override reasoning: OLV 2026 realized 0.34x trailing risk-weighted (P below half 0.96) and LT Trend 0.04x on 23 trades, both 72-75% overflow long (survivorship keep 0.85); OLV's mechanical 1.29 stacked with A-1 and X-3 is what produced the Jun-2026 -$78k to -$96k OLV episode in my composed replay (2016+ maxDD -7.3% -> -9.3% / -11.7%); with OLV at 1.15 and the composite clip (A-1) the 2016+ maxDD returns to -7.5% (Apr-2024, the current book's episode). Replay used LT Trend 1.19; 1.10 is a strict footprint reduction on top and is untested in isolation.
changes.expected_effect: About +4 pts of NAV/yr at 1.3 pts more vol and the same maxDD in the baseline's walk-forward; in my composed replay the tilt alone at GRM 1.5 is Sharpe 2.20 -> 2.30, maxDD -12.4% -> -10.6%, worst 21d -9.5% -> -7.7%, PnL flat (14/22 years better).
changes.confidence: moderate: gate met out of sample; the overrides are judgement on 2026 evidence and survivorship, pending the 2027 Q1 re-read
changes.evidence: dynamic_sizing_plan L1 (1a-1e), study3/study4 results; estimation_haircut_09 (keeps, trust tiers, 2026 per-strategy); practitioner_02 (tilt_only, package A/B/C DD episodes)
changes.intuition: Cut the strategies that own the tail and are best in the most recent era (recency chasing), raise the diversifiers; but a 29% raise on the one strategy that has no stop, stacks in one sector, and just had its worst year is not what a PM does in the year it happened. Give OLV 15% now and the rest when 2027 confirms.
changes.risks: Cap interactions (a raised strategy hits its 250 cap more often) are the P3 confirmation; the tilt applied to history is in-sample for levels; recency variants were worse out of sample so do not switch to them when a strategy's last three years look good.
changes.implementation_notes: process_signals_fast(risk_multipliers=...) confirmation first; then strategy_config base bps per strategy (or a RISK_MULTIPLIERS dict applied at import beside GRM); scan Sizing notes stamp the mult; annual re-fit script in scratch with the numbers in the commit message.

changes.name: OVS: bottom-extremity 0.5x, P2 aggregate cap 0.75% -> 1.5%, keep cycle 0.75x and scale-out
changes.rule: OVS signal sized 0.5x when mean(rank_ret_2d, 5d, 10d, 21d) < 94 at the signal close (no top-tier boost); composes multiplicatively with path, cycle mult, scale-out and caps. path2_daily_cap_pct 0.75 -> 1.5 nominal (2.25% effective at GRM 1.5). cycle_risk_mults {2: 0.75} unchanged. Scale-out 40/60 unchanged.
changes.math: Extremity terciles: T0 avgR +0.18 (N 423, win 0.59) vs T2 +0.51 (N 424); episode-clustered t +5.38 (217 episodes), LOYO 80%, holds in both tiers, both paths and all four eras; fixed cut < 94: N 392 avgR +0.17 vs N 878 +0.47; equal-risk rule +12.9% R per unit risk, 17/24 years, walk-forward tercile form +19.7% (13/18); no-redeploy cost -$36k/24y for a 33% smaller OVS footprint. This clears CLAUDE.md's selectivity bar because the cell is low on EXPECTANCY (+0.17 vs +0.47) as well as win rate, unlike the deleted P(win) meta-labeller. P2 cap: 202 of 609 P2 trades capped, capped avgR +0.37 vs +0.18 uncapped; uncapping to 12 bps effective +$49.5k/24y (8.1% of OVS PnL), worst extra day -$1.4k, 11/14 capping years positive. Cycle: 6/6 midterm years below, year-clustered t -2.00.
changes.expected_effect: OVS PnL per unit risk +13% (extremity) and +$49.5k (P2 cap) over 24y; the freed risk on cluster days goes to higher-extremity P2 rows; the OVS staged-risk footprint falls ~33% on non-cluster days.
changes.confidence: moderate-high on the extremity cut (LOYO 80%, all eras/tiers/paths, mechanism = reversal scales with the prior move); moderate on the P2 cap (cluster-year concentrated)
changes.evidence: signal_quality (findings 1, 3; rules R1-R8; walk-forward); cycle_macro (finding 3, cycle tilt re-confirmed); CLAUDE.md OVS sections
changes.intuition: A vol-spike fade wants the spike to be a real blow-off; a signal that only just clears the 85 rank thresholds is a stock drifting up, not a squeeze ending. Every short desk grades its fades by extremity.
changes.risks: Cut-point 94 chosen after seeing the tables (the walk-forward tercile form is the clean check); engine replay with caps is the confirmation; midterm years flatten the gradient.
changes.implementation_notes: daily_scan sizing step from the same rank_ret_{2,5,10,21}d columns the filter reads; strat_backtester step 3b point-in-time; strategy_config OVS execution 'extremity_derate': {threshold: 94, mult: 0.5}; order_staging needs nothing for the derate, P2 cap constant in order_staging + engine + ledger; tests beside test_ovs_scaleout.py.

changes.name: OLV ladder re-keyed to max(recency rung, depth rung), with a composite clip
changes.rule: mult_OLV = max(recency_rung(ticker, 21td), depth_rung), depth_rung = 0.5 with no OLV legs open (filled OR working), 0.7 with 1-2, 1.0 with 3+. Same-ticker adds stay full size; the 50%-NAV ticker cap stays. Practitioner clip: the PRODUCT of all OLV overlays (tilt x ladder x flow x pullback) is capped at 1.5x base pre-GRM.
changes.math: Current ladder halves 81% of solo legs (0.48R) but also 43-49% of legs entered into 3+ open OLV names (0.93-1.15R). Replays 2005-2026: current $418k / PnL per $ risk 0.790 / exit worst-21d -14.0k; max(recency, depth) $543k / 0.820 / -13.4k, PnL/risk >= current in 15/20 years, +$16k at equal risk; no ladder at all $643k but 0.761 and every tail worse. Sleeve caps, sqrt-n and Kelly-concurrency variants all lose (0.65-0.68). Clip rationale from my composed replay: without it the OLV footprint runs 2.55-2.75x current at GRM 2.25 and Jun-Jul 2026 becomes the decade's worst episode; with tilt 1.15 and the 1.5x clip OLV runs 2.0x at GRM 2.25 (1.35x at 1.5) and the 2016+ maxDD is unchanged from today's.
changes.expected_effect: +$125k/21y raw, +$16k at equal risk, better exit-basis worst-21d and maxDD; MTM maxDD -40.6k -> -54.1k raw is a footprint effect (-43.3k at equal risk).
changes.confidence: moderate (clustered t 1.6-2.0, LOYO floors 1.0-1.5, bootstrap P 0.007-0.017; the ladder remains an appetite cut, only its key changes)
changes.evidence: within_strategy_adds (findings 1, 3, 4; replay variants); dynamic_sizing_plan L2 (OLV stacks are one bet with rising per-leg edge; sleeve cap rejected); practitioner_02 (package A/B vs C OLV episode)
changes.intuition: The second and third names in a sector washout are the better entries, every washout trader knows it; the ladder as shipped punishes exactly those. But OLV has no stop and its clusters are one bet, so the composite must have a ceiling that no combination of overlays can breach.
changes.risks: Depth counted on filled legs; live must count working T+3 limits or the first days of a cluster are under-counted; the 2026-07-29 open-count form was retired for the reset-on-exit bug, so the count must be (open + working), not open alone.
changes.implementation_notes: daily_scan 2c: count open OLV positions + working OLV entries from the sheet/broker book; engine: open_positions state already exists for the ticker cap, add a strategy-level count including unfilled candidates inside their fill window; composite clip as a final min() in the OLV sizing chain in both; tests in test_olv_stop_and_cap.py.

changes.name: Weak Close Decent Sznls and LT Trend ST OS: solo 0.75x, adds 1.25x
changes.rule: mult = 0.75 if no open leg of the same strategy (filled or working), else 1.25. Same-sector clusters are NOT cut. Composes with the frag / P-C bands, the tilt and the 250 cap.
changes.math: WCDS same-day adds 0.73R (N 75, t 2.7, LOYO 2.1, bootstrap P 0.021) vs solo 0.21R (N 156); per signal day 1 fill 0.14R ($579/day) vs 4-5 fills 0.93R ($14.4k/day); replay $337k -> $362k on 5% less risk, PnL/risk 0.281 -> 0.317, MTM maxDD -60.8k -> -55.1k, 18/22 years. LT: 3-5 open 0.63R (N 25, t 2.65, LOYO 2.0, P 0.009) vs solo 0.22R; replay $233k -> $242k on 4% less risk, PnL/risk 0.301 -> 0.327, worst-21d -15.5k -> -12.5k, maxDD -21.2k -> -19.1k; at dial 65+ the cluster adds are the only LT legs with edge (0.63R vs solo -0.12R). Cluster days for WCDS 2016+: mean dial 15.6, 0% at >= 50.
changes.expected_effect: +$63k at equal risk over the two, with both sleeves' maxDD and worst-21d better; the cap binds on 7-9 days each at 1.25x.
changes.confidence: moderate
changes.evidence: within_strategy_adds (finding 6); flow_conditional (dip_buy / oversold_hold flow effect, same sign)
changes.intuition: One weak close in one sector ETF is noise; five weak closes across sectors on the same day is a washout, and the desk wants to be bigger in the washout, not smaller.
changes.risks: Small LT cells; WCDS Size_Mult still carries a legacy seasonal tilt the replay left in place.
changes.implementation_notes: Generic per-strategy open-count derate/up-rate keyed on (open + working) legs; the dormant ladder machinery (execution['ladder_multipliers'], load_open_position_counts) can carry it as [0.75, 1.25, 1.25] if its key is per-strategy; engine pre-pass mirrors A-1's count; tests.

changes.name: 52wh Breakout: 0.5x at >= 6 open legs (tail insurance), not >= 5
changes.rule: mult = 0.5 when the strategy has >= 6 open 52wh legs at entry; labelled variance/tail insurance with a re-exam at +15 legs in the cell; retire if the cell's avgR >= 0.4 then. The plan's >= 5 threshold is withdrawn.
changes.math: 2010+: exact-5 open 1.71R (N 13, $87.6k) vs >= 6 open 0.08R (N 23, 35% win); full-history >= 6 vs rest -0.10R, bootstrap P 0.57 (not an edge claim); the >= 6 cell owns 88% of 52wh's worst 21d MTM window (Feb-2014 -$59.5k, 10 of 15 legs open). Replays: >= 5 at 0.5x -$68.5k raw and -$9.4k at equal risk (cuts the 1.71R cell); >= 6 at 0.5x -$34.6k raw (almost all pre-2010), +$7.5k at equal risk, sleeve worst-21d -59.5k -> -33.3k, MTM maxDD -78k -> -61k.
changes.expected_effect: Halves the Feb-2014-type window at near-zero equal-risk cost; raw cost ~$1.5k/yr.
changes.confidence: low on the edge, high that >= 5 is the wrong threshold
changes.evidence: within_strategy_adds (finding 7); dynamic_sizing_plan L2 (52wh 7-12 legs -$36/leg-day); cycle_macro (52wh loses in rolling-over tape, dial >= 50 Sharpe -2.2 while it cannot enter)
changes.intuition: The sixth simultaneous breakout is late-cycle; the exit question (P4) matters more than this sizing one and stays on the list.
changes.risks: Era-dependent, 4 post-2010 episodes; the P4 exit rule may make it moot.
changes.implementation_notes: Same open-count mechanism as A-2 with mults [1,1,1,1,1,1,0.5] or a threshold form; engine parity trivial.

changes.name: Index clone clamps: IOB SPY+QQQ 0.5x each, dip-buy same-ticker cross-strategy clamps
changes.rule: Indices Oversold Bounce SPY and QQQ firing the same day size 0.5x each; extend CROSS_STRATEGY_OVERLAP_OVERRIDES (20 bps nominal per side, GRM-scaled) to every dip-buy pair (Monday Dip + WCDS, MonFri + WCDS, Monthly WC + MonFri) on the same ticker and day. MonFri's SPY+QQQ pairs untouched (its both-fire days earn 3.1x at 2.1x sd).
changes.math: IOB both-fire days: 50 of 133 signal days, leg-R corr 0.88, mean 1.9x a single-leg day at 2.3x the sd; 14 cross-strategy same-ticker pairs since 2010 with R corr 0.97. Variance-only: -$1.3k/yr expected on the IOB cell.
changes.expected_effect: Both-day sd cut 2.3x -> 1.15x on IOB clone days; no expected-value content; also reduces the SPY > 50% NAV single-ticker days that drive the margin peak (GM-2).
changes.confidence: high (rho ~1 clamps have no edge content)
changes.evidence: dynamic_sizing_plan L2 decisions 1-2, study2 clones
changes.intuition: Two tickets on one horse.
changes.risks: None material.
changes.implementation_notes: Existing overlap-clamp machinery (daily_scan 5b, engine 3b3c candidate pre-pass) keyed within IOB; new pairs in strategy_config; guard test.

changes.name: No correlation-, sector-, same-ticker- or stack-age-keyed cuts anywhere; no Kelly-concurrency per-leg rule; no OLV sleeve budget
changes.rule: Add sizing is keyed on marginal expected R only. Ex-ante rho63 with open names, same-sector counts, same-ticker counts (OLV) and stack age may be displayed, never sized on. The OLV sleeve open-risk cap and the retired 100%-NAV OLV book cap stay retired; the OLV 50%-NAV ticker cap stays as catastrophe insurance.
changes.math: Spearman(R, rho63) among adds -0.04 to +0.16; rho > 0.6 cuts lose PnL per $ risk in OLV (0.790 -> 0.762), OVS, WCDS, LT, 3x ETF; same-sector 2+ cuts lose everywhere they bind (OLV -> 0.732); OLV same-ticker adds are its best cell (0.98R, 1.92R at 3+ deep, 7/7 wins); Kelly-concurrency edge/(1+n rho) OLV 0.651 vs 0.790; sleeve caps 250-400 bps cost $28-70k/16y for $3.4k of worst-21d.
changes.expected_effect: Avoids measured losses of 0.02-0.14 PnL per $ risk per strategy.
changes.confidence: high
changes.evidence: within_strategy_adds (findings 2, 3, negatives); dynamic_sizing_plan L2 (OLV budget rejected)
changes.intuition: At 6-13% of Kelly the variance tax on a correlated leg is second order and the clones are the best legs; concentration is handled by the factor hedge and the margin guard, not by per-leg cuts.
changes.risks: Concentration in a no-stop stack is real; GM-2, GM-5 and the ticker cap are the controls that survive the evidence.
changes.implementation_notes: Negative-registry entries; nothing to build.

changes.name: Dial-armed whole-book beta hedge in MES: paper-track one episode, then ship
changes.rule: Arm when the lag-1 10d-MA 63d dial >= 50, release below 45 (hysteresis). Target = whole-book flat-basis MTM beta. Instrument MES (never NQ, never RTY). beta_hat = 126-session lag-1 OLS of book return on SPY, clipped [-1, 2], refreshed daily (or the 0.5 x 63d + 0.5 x expanding blend); ratio 1.0x, never above 1.5x. Contracts = beta_hat x base / (5 x ES). Native MOC entry (orderType MOC / tif DAY per the 2026-08-21 rule), quarterly roll on the panel's schedule, 2 bps friction budgeted per arm. Second-stage sensitivity pre-registered now: arming gate dial >= 50 AND VIX < 20 with forced release at VIX >= 30, adopted only if it is not worse than plain 50/45 over the next two out-of-sample episodes. Score on the PIT vintage; log arm/release, beta_126, beta_63, armed-day SPY drift on the panel.
changes.math: PIT vintage 2018-2026, 50/45: 544 armed days, 13 episodes, +$104k (2.56 bps/armed day), 10/13 episodes positive, clustered t 1.68, Sharpe 2.90 -> 3.04, maxDD -8.32% -> -8.13%, bootstrap P(<= 0) 0.046, placebo rank 1.000, LOYO 7/9; 126d beta +$110k, Sharpe 3.07, maxDD -7.89%. Live vintage +$35k t 0.72. 65/60 is a Feb-2020 result (t 0.99, drop-best t 0.37). Mechanism: book beta is HIGHEST in calm near-the-highs tape (VIX < 15 beta 0.52, R2 0.21) and LOWEST after vol arrives (VIX 30+ beta 0.17, book Sharpe 3.8); the dial fires in the complacent pre-selloff state where SPY's conditional drift is negative (-24% ann at 65+); VIX-, VIX-percentile- and drawdown-armed hedges all lose (-$139k to -$158k). In my package replay the same hedge on the package series adds +$25-33k on 409 armed days (2016-07+), Sharpe +0.05, and improves the 2016+ maxDD -7.5% -> -6.9% at GRM 1.5, -9.4% -> -8.7% at 1.875. Sub-book targets earn one third to two thirds of the whole-book hedge because at high dial the factor sits in LT Trend / 52wh / St OS Sznl, not FAMILY4.
changes.expected_effect: ~1.3 episodes/yr, ~+$8k per episode, +0.1 to +0.15 full-sample Sharpe, calm carry limited to false alarms (~4 in 10 episodes, ~-$5k/yr); does NOT reduce book variance (armed sd 80.6 -> 76.0 bps) and does NOT relieve margin (futures margin is additive).
changes.confidence: moderate: passes the written ship rule on PIT with margin (t 1.68 vs 1.0), 13 episodes, drift-driven; the VIX-gated variant is in-sample over 12 variants and every t there is inflated by about one unit
changes.evidence: cross_strategy_regime (findings 1-8, hedge grid, PIT rebuild); dynamic_sizing_plan L3 / P1; practitioner_02 hedged rows; outside: Daniel-Moskowitz 2016 (ex-ante beta hedges of state-dependent-beta strategies fail; use a bear-state term), Longin-Solnik 2001 (correlation rises with bear trend, not vol), CFM 2024 (dip-buy returns are mostly embedded beta)
changes.intuition: This is the systematic form of the August 2026 hand hedge, and the only dial-conditioned control in the repo that acts on what the dial forecasts (SPY drift and the book's factor share) rather than on book variance. The outside literature warns that trailing-beta hedges under-hedge the loss side and sell the rebound; that is why the ratio is 1.0x of a slow beta, the release is fast, and the VIX gate is registered as the next test rather than shipped.
changes.risks: The dial was calibrated on SPY forward returns (PIT cures weight lookahead only); 2018 PIT is a one-signal vintage; the book's up-beta (0.50-0.79) exceeds its down-beta (0.27) so a full hedge gives back more on rallies than it saves per unit move; execution: MES must be MOC-native, and the panel must net it against GM-3's futures legs.
changes.implementation_notes: Hedge panel arm/release state + beta computation in build_betas.py; a hedge runner in trading_ibkr (event_moo-style, clientId of its own, orderRef 'MES|SELL|Book_Hedge|date'); daily_risk_report prints the armed state; prereg doc updated with the VIX-gate second stage and its decision rule.

changes.name: Dial bands: keep FAMILY4 / 3x Bear / Monthly WC bands and the P/C-fear tables; LT Trend ST OS [[50,999,0.5]] on PIT as a gated candidate; OLV and OVS stay exempt; drop the 65 re-test
changes.rule: No change to frag_risk_bands or PC_FEAR_BANDS today. Run P2 at the 50 line on the PIT series (not 65): adopt LT Trend ST OS plain [[50, 999, 0.5]] only if PIT clustered t <= -2.0 (have -2.33 on 9 episodes), survives drop-best-episode (have -0.34) and LOYO all negative (have -0.48..-0.28); re-exam at +2 hi-dial episodes, retire if episode signs fall below 5/11. Replace the plan's L3 current-weights trade table with the PIT table (book 65+ cell is +0.006R vs < 50 on PIT, t 0.04; OLV +0.235R). Once X-1 is live, re-open the FAMILY4 0.25x band as a prereg question scored on HEDGED returns.
changes.math: On PIT weights the plan's 50-65 'sweet spot' (+0.204, t 1.53) and 65+ 'edge halves' (-0.171, t -1.20) both vanish (PIT -0.141 t -0.91 and +0.006 t +0.04). LT Trend PIT >= 50: 0.107 (N 62) vs 0.482 (N 87), diff -0.375, t -2.33, 1 pos/5 neg years, single-strategy WF PPR +14% 5/6 years, strategy Sharpe 1.00 -> 1.14, maxDD -2.25 -> -1.43; book effect +$47k risk-matched over 8y. In my composed replay the LT dial cut adds +0.005 PnL/risk and nothing to the tails (current-weights proxy). The FAMILY4 band on PIT: hi -0.10 vs lo +0.63, t -1.96, negative in 6 of 9 years; outside evidence (Nagel 2012) says single-name liquidity provision earns MORE in high-VIX tape, which is why the P/C-fear ON branch (full size in washouts) is the evidence-aligned half and the band's OFF-state zeroing is the part to re-test on hedged returns.
changes.expected_effect: LT Trend: small in dollars; its value is removing the one exemption that fails on PIT. FAMILY4 re-test: unknown; nothing changes now.
changes.confidence: moderate-low on LT Trend (5 of 9 episodes negative, two big ones carry 28 of 62 trades); high on the OLV/OVS exemptions (PIT null) and on dropping the 65 line
changes.evidence: cycle_macro (finding 5, PIT rebuild); signal_quality (finding 5: OLV dial gradient is a current-weights artefact, PIT t +0.03); cross_strategy_regime (band-vs-hedge convexity argument: beta_up 0.79 vs beta_down 0.26 at 65+); CLAUDE.md fragility contract (freeze policy, prereg requirement); outside: Nagel 2012
changes.intuition: A trend dip-buy is the strategy most exposed to a fragile-at-highs distribution rolling over (its daily beta per active day 0.27, highest of the exempt three), so the LT cut is the one that makes sense mechanically; the OLV dial band was retired for the right reason.
changes.risks: Dial rows before 2026-07-02 are the recompute vintage; the PIT series ends 2026-05-07 so Aug-2026 is current-weights only; LT cells are 3-48 legs.
changes.implementation_notes: Prereg doc update (P2 at 50 on PIT); if adopted, strategy_config LT Trend execution frag_risk_bands (plain table, NOT P/C-conditioned since LT is not a FAMILY4 carrier), engine 3b3 and scan 2b already generic; test_frag_risk_bands.py.

changes.name: OLV pullback tilt: 1.25x when SPY is 3-10% off its 252d high at the signal close
changes.rule: execution['market_state_bands'] for Oversold Low Volume: SPY close / rolling-252d high - 1 in [-10%, -3%) -> 1.25x (half of the fitted 1.5x); at-highs side stays 1.0x (do not cut the < 3% cell, it is still +0.56R). Composes with the recency/depth ladder, earnings override and ticker cap, inside the A-1 composite clip. Ship rule already met in the study: clustered t >= 1.5 on 2010+ (have 2.98) and >= 10 of 15 WF years better (have 11).
changes.math: OLV x SPY drawdown 3-10%: avgR 1.184 (N 103) vs 0.554 rest, t 2.98, 8 pos / 1 neg years, survives Size_Mult >= 0.99 and dial < 50 subsets; < 3% cell 0.562 (N 211). Single-strategy WF 2010-2026: PPR 0.796 -> 0.885 (+11.3%), 11/15 years, OLV Sharpe 1.33 -> 1.36, maxDD -2.75 -> -2.33. Fixed 1.5x: 16/17 years, book Sharpe 2.515 -> 2.553, +$74k risk-matched. Mechanism: liquidity-provision premium scales with stress (Nagel), and the dial is almost never >= 50 in a 3-10% pullback (P = 0.7-5%), so the two controls act on disjoint days. In my composed replay the tilt alone is +1.4% PnL at GRM 1.875 with maxDD unchanged, 16/22 years.
changes.expected_effect: +7-11% OLV PnL per unit risk, ~+$50k risk-matched over 16y at the half tilt; OLV open risk rises only in pullbacks where its stacks are currently shallow (flow 19.9/yr at 3-10 vs 16.2 at < 3).
changes.confidence: moderate
changes.evidence: cycle_macro (finding 6, recommendation 2); signal_quality (OLV market-pullback tiers: beta channel caveat, OLV-alone WF on spy_hi252 failed for the CUT side); outside: Nagel 2012, Daniel-Moskowitz loser up-betas
changes.intuition: OLV buys quiet washouts; when the whole tape is 5% off its high the washouts are real and the recovery has a market tailwind. The at-highs OLV trade is the beta-less version and it still works, so no cut there.
changes.risks: Partly a beta channel (SPY fwd10 +1.25% off-high vs +0.46% near-high): if X-1 is armed the two overlap only when the dial is high in a pullback, which is rare; ~900 regime cells were scanned in that study and this one is cited because it has a mechanism, LOYO and walk-forward.
changes.implementation_notes: Generic 'market_state_bands' hook (SPY 252d-high distance from master_prices, PIT by construction) in daily_scan sizing and engine 3b; strategy_config OLV execution; test.

changes.name: Momentum-factor and effective-N exposure: display, never size
changes.rule: Show the book's 12-1 momentum loading, rolling 126d effective N and n_active on the hedge panel (GM-7). No sizing on correlation spikes, effective-N collapses or signal-cluster days.
changes.math: Momentum loading t 8.1 all-sample (carriers OLV, 3x Fade, 52wh, LTT), ~15% of book variance at dial >= 50; rolling eff N uncorrelated with the dial (Spearman -0.02) and VIX (+0.05), its lows are single-sleeve dominance events; days with 5-6 active strategies have beta 1.13 and Sharpe 4.7 (58 bps/day), trailing-5d signal count > 15 has Sharpe 4.15.
changes.expected_effect: Preserves the days that carry the edge; makes the un-hedged momentum-crash exposure visible.
changes.confidence: high
changes.evidence: cross_strategy_regime (findings 6, 7)
changes.intuition: The cluster days are the paydays; a PM who de-risks on 'correlations are rising' during a washout sells the bottom.
changes.risks: Momentum factor built from survivors; use its loadings, not its mean.
changes.implementation_notes: GM-7 panel.

changes.name: Up-only family flow multiplier 1.25x, dial-gated for dip-buys, headroom-gated for all
changes.rule: New sizing step after 2b (frag band) and before the recency/depth ladder: mult = 1.25 when the family's trailing-5d RAW candidate count (inclusive of today, counted from the same filter masks daily_scan evaluates, BEFORE earnings blackout / T+1 gates / fill windows) >= threshold: dip_buy >= 6 AND 10d-MA 63d dial < 50; oversold_hold >= 7; short_fade >= 104. No breakout carrier. No down-size leg (the 0.75x low-flow half is optional variance funding and costs PnL). Switched off for the day by GM-2 when the projected requirement > 60% of live NLV. Post-ship review pre-registered: PnL/risk on the first 60 hi-flow trades >= 1.3x the concurrent lo/mid-flow trades, else retire.
changes.math: Flow terciles within family 2005-2026: dip_buy avgR 0.216 / 0.657 / 0.569 (PnL per risk 0.212 -> 0.572, episode t 2.70), oversold_hold 0.317 / 0.571 / 0.855 (t 3.00), short_fade 0.298 / 0.367 / 0.678 (t 3.21); per-year Spearman positive in 82-84% of 22 years; survives VIX, trend, realized vol, drawdown and dial controls; dip_buy effect absent at dial >= 30 (hence the gate). Fixed up-only rule 2010-2026, cap re-applied: book PnL +5.0% at +4.2% risk, Sharpe flat (2.197), maxDD -$92.9k -> -$102.8k, 17/17 years better, worst year +1%; walk-forward fitted form +10.4% PnL, Sharpe 2.20 -> 2.25, 15/17. In my composed replay the flow layer alone at GRM 1.5: PnL +10% ($3.51M -> $3.86M), Sharpe 2.20 -> 2.23, 22/22 years better, but maxDD -12.4% -> -13.7% and worst day -5.9% -> -6.8%, and the peak requirement day rises 0.61 -> 0.80 of base because the hi-flow days ARE the peak-gross days; the guard exists for that. NEW supporting evidence (practitioner_01): the 5 sessions after a worst-5% book day average +135 bps vs +40 (t 2.8), i.e. the post-hit window is when flow is high and the book is best paid.
changes.expected_effect: +5% book PnL for +4% risk at Sharpe flat (up-only), ~+10% combined with F-2; it is a growth / PnL-per-risk lever, not a Sharpe lever, exactly the kind of appetite decision the brief invites.
changes.confidence: moderate: expectancy evidence strong (t 2.7-3.3, 82-84% of years, two flow sources, controls), rule Sharpe-neutral because high-flow legs are one correlated bet; the sizing pack's 'size DOWN on high flow' hypothesis is wrong-signed in every mean-reverting family
changes.evidence: flow_conditional (findings 1-5, fixed rules, walk-forward); seasonality_flow (finding 5: OVS 5+ vs <5 0.648 vs 0.230, q 0.002, LOYO floor +0.335; book 5+ signals 0.70 vs 0.42); signal_quality (finding 2: pooled t +3.90, 10/13 strategies); practitioner_01 (post-hit forward returns); practitioner_02 (flow_only rows)
changes.intuition: When everything is firing the tape is dislocated and the liquidity premium is on the table; that is when a desk presses. The one honest caveat from the same data is that pressing on those days is also when the margin sheet is tightest, so the press is conditional on headroom, never on conviction.
changes.risks: Thresholds are the 2026 expanding-window terciles (in-sample level, out-of-sample multipliers); flow must be counted from raw candidate masks live (staged-row counts would shift every threshold, OVS runs ~16x its fills); the composed replay stacked this on OLV without the clip and produced the Jun-2026 episode, so ship only with A-1's clip.
changes.implementation_notes: daily_scan: per-family raw candidate counts from filters.live_signal_mask over the trailing 5 sessions (cache the daily counts in data/ like the dial), stamped into Sizing notes and a per-day family flag column for order_staging (GM-5 relief reads it); engine: candidate pre-pass count per family-day from generate_candidates_fast (the flow study's method, engine == scan); strategy_config FAMILY map + FLOW_THRESHOLDS as source of truth; tests for count parity and the dial gate.

changes.name: Flow-aware per-strategy cap relief (250 -> 375 on the family's hi-flow days)
changes.rule: See GM-5: cap x1.5 on any day the strategy's family is in its F-1 hi-flow state, taking the MAX with the OVS 375 rule (never the product), off when GM-2's projected requirement > 60% of live NLV. Breakout family excluded (the cap never binds there).
changes.math: Cap binds on 20.9% of trades (130 strategy-days), in the top flow tercile 11.8% dip_buy / 25.7% oversold_hold / 78.0% short_fade of trades; re-applying the cap removes 15% / 25% / 83% of a 1.25x up-size. Relief x1.5 on hi-flow days, 2010-2026: dip_buy +$31k (+2.4%) Sharpe 1.521 -> 1.542, maxDD and worst-21d identical; short_fade +$77k (+8.3%) Sharpe 1.177 -> 1.184, tails identical; oversold_hold +$21k, Sharpe 1.327 -> 1.301; book +3.8% PnL, +2.0% risk, Sharpe 2.199 -> 2.222, maxDD -$92,866 vs -$92,867, 10/17 years better and 7 identical. x2.0 leaves maxDD identical too but x99 blows the OVS tail. In my composed replay relief is worth about +$200k over 16y at GRM 1.5 (package C $3.92M vs no-relief $3.72M) at Sharpe 2.38 vs 2.36 and identical maxDD/worst-day, but it moved the peak requirement day from 0.60 to 0.88 of base when stacked with the OVS 375 (the non-stacked rule removes that).
changes.expected_effect: +3.8% book PnL with Sharpe up and tails byte-identical (single-overlay study); the cleanest flow rule in the study because it acts on the cap, not the base bps.
changes.confidence: moderate-high (unfitted, mechanical mechanism, tails unchanged); verify live placed totals vs ledger-implied before shipping
changes.evidence: flow_conditional (finding 6, recommendation 1); within_strategy_adds (OVS cap replay); practitioner_02 (package C vs package C_no_relief; stacked peak day)
changes.intuition: The cap binds on the avgR-0.62 OVS days and the 0.96 Weak Close days; loosening it 50% on the days the family is firing is how you let the book's best days be its best days without giving up the 2021-01-27 protection.
changes.risks: Same fills at larger size (no impact modelled on 9+ signal OVS days); P2 aggregate cap interaction not replayed.
changes.implementation_notes: GM-5 sites; the family flag comes from F-1's scanner stamp.

changes.name: OVS same-day cluster tilt: pre-register only
changes.rule: Candidate: when the PM scan stages >= 5 OVS signals, size each at 1.25x (P1 and P2) inside the 375 cap. Decision rule written before the run: episode-clustered t >= 2 on the 5+ vs < 5 gap with the 2026 episodes included, LOYO gap floor > +0.20, no worst-day deterioration beyond 0.5 pt in the replay, P1/P2 split reported separately. Not shipped from this study; F-2 already covers most of the cell through the short_fade relief.
changes.math: Same-day OVS count: 1 signal avgR 0.193 (N 436), 5+ 0.648 vs < 5 0.230 (R/risk 0.52 vs ~0.30), episode t 4.84, q 0.002, 29 episodes / 38 days, LOYO floor +0.335, 10/11 years positive (2026: -0.17 on 18 fills; Feb-3 and Jun-24 2026 cluster days lost -0.90 / -1.10); ledger risk on 5+ days median 93 bps, none at the cap (the P2 12-bps rows and P2 aggregate cap keep them small).
changes.expected_effect: +$1-2k per cluster day on ~2 days a year; episode-concentrated (7 dates carry the 16+ bucket).
changes.confidence: moderate on the cell, low on shipping (29 episodes, both 2026 clusters lost)
changes.evidence: seasonality_flow (finding 5, recommendation 3); within_strategy_adds (OVS depth cells)
changes.intuition: A 16-signal OVS day is a market-wide blow-off reversing; the fades work because the whole tape is turning. But the two 2026 cluster days lost and the desk rule is 'the market gets a vote before I add'.
changes.risks: Do not generalise to 52wh (opposite stack effect) or to the bear fade's same_day derate.
changes.implementation_notes: Prereg doc; data already in the scanner (same-day count).

changes.name: No flow rule for breakouts; no size-down on flow anywhere; keep the 3x Bear same-day derate and the OLV recency ladder direction
changes.rule: 52wh Breakout and Sector BO get no family multiplier and no cap relief (A-3 is their only flow-shaped control). No strategy gets a 'crowded selloff' cut. 3x Bear ETF Overbot Fade keeps same_day_signal_derate as a variance rule only.
changes.math: Breakout: 17 flow variables, cluster t between -1.5 and +1.0, every replayed form at or below baseline Sharpe (0.87 base, 0.81-0.85), f21_rel +11% PnL with maxDD -$82k -> -$106k. Down-only 0.75x on low flow costs 5.7% book PnL for 9.1% less risk. 3x Bear same-day cells 0.64 / 0.37 / 0.85 (no gradient, N 30/9/16).
changes.expected_effect: Avoids wrong-signed cuts on the best legs of every mean-reverting family.
changes.confidence: high
changes.evidence: flow_conditional (negatives, recommendation 4-5)
changes.intuition: Breakout clusters are late-cycle (the sixth breakout fails) so the only flow control there is the deep-stack insurance; reversal clusters are early-cycle so you press.
changes.risks: None.
changes.implementation_notes: Negative-registry entries.

changes.name: No calendar-conditional sizing layer of any kind; codify the closed list
changes.rule: No multiplier may reference month, quarter, half-year, earnings season, opex week, turn-of-month, day-of-week or holiday adjacency. The GRM frontier is computed on the whole-year series and never per season. Earnings handling stays per-name (OVS +-10 td blackout, OLV / St OS Sznl pre-print overrides), never per-season. Register as closed: September 0.5x, Aug-Sep 0.75x, May-Oct 0.75x, Nov-Apr 1.25x, December 1.25x, Q4 1.25x, opex-week dip-buy cut, turn-of-month tilts, holiday tilts, OLV August cut, LT Trend June cut, 52wh October boost, OVS December boost, January de-rate, Friday de-rate, single-stock earnings-season 0.75x.
changes.math: 1,012 strategy x calendar cells on year-clustered tests: zero BH-FDR survivors in every dimension (min q 0.27), zero Bonferroni; fitted calendar multipliers <= baseline OOS in 17 of 18 rule/design combinations, the one positive (strat x month WF +0.04 Sharpe, t 1.0) reverses under LOYO (-0.056, maxDD 2.6 pts worse). Unfitted priors replayed: Sep 0.5x -4.5% PnL (1/24 years better), May-Oct 0.75x -11.3% with maxDD unchanged, Nov-Apr 1.25x +13.7% PnL but Sharpe -0.033 and maxDD -3.0 pts, earnings-season single-stock 0.75x -7.1% (0-1 of 17-24 years). Seasonal variance IS real (May-Oct sd 63 vs 83 bps/day, t -3.19) but so is the mean (7.1 vs 11.6 bps, t -2.67): Kelly ratio summer/winter 1.06 pooled, median 1.03; sd tracks open risk (Spearman 0.77, elasticity 0.51), so the summer 'low vol, add leverage' move is the mistake a vol target would make. Earnings season is BETTER after the blackouts (book 0.560 vs 0.430, 14/15 strategies same sign, LOYO positive for single-stock strategies).
changes.expected_effect: Zero PnL change; avoids the -1% to -11% PnL and 0 to -3 pt maxDD outcomes of every replayed calendar rule and the 1,000-cell garden of forking paths.
changes.confidence: high
changes.evidence: seasonality_flow (all findings, negatives); cross_strategy_regime (month cells 16 observations each); outside calendar pack (TOM decayed post-2015, Halloween insignificant for S&P 1984-2009, pre-holiday gone for large caps, Monday effect dead, pre-FOMC drift gone since 2015; McLean-Pontiff decay on calendar cells)
changes.intuition: Twenty years says the calendar stories are about the index, and this book trades conditional entries with ATR exits; the index drift does not describe the conditional cell. The one place the calendar shows up is FLOW (WCDS December 2.2x, OVS July 0.5x) and flow is already the sizing state.
changes.risks: Small strategies have 1-14 trades per month cell: absence of evidence there is a power statement; the dip-buy summer watch (SZ-2) is the one open item.
changes.implementation_notes: CLAUDE.md negative-registry section; nothing to build.

changes.name: Dip-buy family in May-Oct: full size, written watch item
changes.rule: No change now. Watch: if the family's expanding May-Oct minus Nov-Apr gap stays below -0.15 AND the September dip-buy cell (currently R/risk 0.03, N 70) is <= 0 after 20 more September fills (~2029), re-open a 0.75x September-only appetite decision. No Nov-Apr boost for dip-buys unless GRM rises book-wide.
changes.math: Dip-buy core May-Oct avgR 0.301 (R/risk 0.298, N 486) vs Nov-Apr 0.494 (0.476, N 600), episode t -2.12, year-paired t -1.79, LOYO gap [-0.25, -0.14], 6/6 members same sign, non-family control opposite-signed; but the gap only appeared after 2013 (positive through 2012) and the summer cell still earns +0.30 R/risk at 6-13% of Kelly, so the replay of a 0.75x cut is -3.1% PnL for zero maxDD change (6/24 years better), and the walk-forward self-gated version -0.35%.
changes.expected_effect: None now.
changes.confidence: moderate that the effect is real, high that a cut does not pay
changes.evidence: seasonality_flow (finding 4, recommendation 5); outside: Bouman-Jacobsen / Jacobsen-Zhang (Halloween), Hong-Yu (summer liquidity), Dichtl-Drobetz (post-publication weakening)
changes.intuition: Summer tape is thinner and the dips are shallower; you notice it, you do not size on it at +0.30 R per unit risk.
changes.risks: Survivorship flatters the winter cell more than the summer cell.
changes.implementation_notes: Watch-list entry with the two numbers and the 2029 date.

seasonality_rules: Rule 0 (sizing): nothing in the sizing chain references the calendar. Every seasonal statement below is an execution, attention or research rule, never a multiplier (evidence: 0 of 1,012 calendar cells survive year-clustered FDR; every fitted or unfitted calendar overlay is at or below baseline OOS).

Flow is the seasonal variable, not the month: December (book flow 1.50x, WCDS 2.2x, OVS 1.9x), January (1.26x) and June (1.27x) are high-flow months with AVERAGE per-signal quality (book avgR 0.45-0.49 vs 0.47), so the F-1/F-2 flow rules will naturally run bigger then and smaller in July-October (flow 0.79-0.83x). Expect the book's realized vol to be seasonal for that reason (May-Oct sd 63 vs Nov-Apr 83 bps/day) and do not let a vol target or a 'quiet summer' instinct add leverage: mean falls with vol in proportion (Kelly ratio 1.03).

Earnings seasons are BETTER for every strategy after the per-name blackouts (book avgR 0.56 vs 0.43; single-stock strategies 7/7 same sign, LOYO positive): keep the OVS +-10 td blackout and the OLV / St OS Sznl pre-print overrides (jump risk on no-stop holders, So-Wang 6x reversal-with-jump-risk), never add a season-wide haircut, and do not relax the blackouts either; the OLV post-print <= 21 td cell (+0.38 vs +0.90, LOYO 60%) is the near-miss to re-examine at +20 trades, the pre-print cell shows no deficit.

Midterm years: OVS stays at 0.75x (6/6 midterm years below, year-clustered t -2.00); no book-wide midterm cut (Sharpe-neutral, risk-matched maxDD 0.5 pt worse). Read 2026's 0.52x realized edge as the midterm base rate (midterm Jan-Aug windows average 0.27 vs 0.52 non-midterm), not as decay, and re-read OLV and LT Trend ST OS in 2027 Q1 (first non-midterm quarters) before restoring their full tilt raises.

September: not a bad month for this book (book avgR 0.418, positive PnL 15/23 years, daily Sharpe 2.21, only 3 drawdown troughs); the only zero-expectancy September cell is the dip-buy family (R/risk 0.03, N 70) and it is a watch item with a 2029 trigger (SZ-2), not a rule. The September post-opex weakness is already the event sleeve's T3 IWM short; never add a second September short.

January is the book's highest-variance month (sd 96 bps, ratio 1.36) but the excess is episodic (8 of 24 Januaries, median ratio 0.99) and coincides with high open risk into a selloff (2008, 2015, 2016, 2021, 2022): that is the dial hedge's territory (X-1) and the headroom guard's (GM-2), not a January de-rate. Watch the panel's gross/NLV in the first two weeks of January.

Turn-of-month and opex week: no sizing rule (book TOM 0.404 vs 0.488, p 0.19; opex 0.450 vs 0.475, p 0.63; replays -7.0% for a book TOM cut, -1.2% for an opex dip-buy cut). Execution note only: US settlement moved to T+1 on 2024-05-28, so any month-end selling-pressure analogue (Etula et al) is now anchored at T-1 not T-3; if the pitch or context products cite the old window, re-anchor.

Day of week: Friday MTM is weak for the book (3.6 vs 10.3 bps/day, worse in 21/24 years) but it is a holding-day effect (MonFri / Monday Dip structurally flat on Fridays, OVS T+2 exits) and Friday SIGNALS are fine (0.564 vs 0.45-0.49): nothing for sizing. If anything is ever tested it is an OVS exit-day question, pre-registered.

Quarter-end and futures roll: the MES hedge (X-1) and any GM-3 index legs roll on the panel's schedule the week before expiry; never carry a hedge into the roll unmanaged, and never let a roll fall on a day the guard says headroom is under 70%.

Holiday and half-session tape: no sizing tilt (pre-holiday avgR 0.386 vs 0.471, p 0.37; sessions are quieter, sd 59 vs 74, same mean). Execution rule: MOC-style exits and event-sleeve auction orders on half-days use the early-close cutoffs the runners already encode; check the calendar the day before.

narrative: Where I come out, and why. The honest summary of the whole evidence pack is that this book has three real levers and one real wall. The levers are the growth multiplier (linear all the way to 3x current size), signal flow (the best days are the days everything fires, in every mean-reverting family, and the caps currently fight that), and reallocation inside and across strategies toward the legs and strategies that own PnL rather than tail (cluster adds, OVS's extreme signals, the diversifiers; away from 52wh, Sector BO, WCDS, IOB base size and OVS's marginal signals). The wall is the broker: on the historical peak day the current book already needs 61% of the sizing base and 72% of live NLV in margin at plain portfolio-margin rates, and that day is a long dip-buy cluster on index ETFs, which is also the book's best kind of day. Nothing about drawdown enters the GRM decision; the drawdown is an output I am willing to read off the table (median 7-9%, p95 12-18%, a 20-25% year inside expectation at Sharpe 2 and 15% vol), and the ACF work this session says cutting into one is the wrong trade. Two things the single-overlay studies could not see, which I built this session. First, composition: every evidenced overlay is an up-size on the same legs on the same days. Stacked as proposed, the OLV tilt (1.29) times the depth ladder times the pullback tilt times the flow boost turns the June-July 2026 oil cluster into the worst episode of the decade (-$96k on OLV alone, 2016+ maxDD -7.3% to -11.7%). With the practitioner clip (OLV tilt 1.15, OLV product capped at 1.5x pre-GRM) and the headroom guard (no up-size when the current book's gross is already past 2x NAV) the same package at today's GRM is +12% PnL, Sharpe 2.20 to 2.38, maxDD -12.4% to -10.0%, worst 21 days -9.5% to -6.4%, 17 of 22 years better, with the 2016+ worst episode back to April 2024 where the current book's is. Second, the reliefs: the OVS 375 cap and the family flow relief multiplied together (562 bps) moved the peak margin day to the 2023-02-03 OVS cluster at 88% of base; taken as a max they do not. Press / pull-in playbook, as a desk would run it. PRESS: (1) when a family's 5-day raw candidate count crosses its threshold (dip-buys with the dial under 50, oversold-holds, short-fades) the base bps run 1.25x and the strategy cap 375, provided the projected requirement is under 60% of live NLV; (2) OLV when SPY is 3-10% off its high, 1.25x; (3) the second, third and fourth legs of a WCDS / LT / OLV cluster, 1.25x or full rung, the clones included; (4) OVS on extreme signals and on cluster days inside 375 bps; (5) the five sessions after a worst-5% book day, which is when flow is high and the book is best paid: hold size, let the flow rule raise it, never cut; (6) earnings season, at full size, because the per-name blackouts already removed the bad cell. PULL IN: (1) at fragile highs, through the family bands and the P/C-fear tables that exist, plus the dial-armed MES hedge at 50/45 once it has paper-tracked an episode; the hedge, not a cut, because the book's convexity (up-beta 0.79 vs down-beta 0.26 at high dial) is worth keeping; (2) OVS signals that only just clear the rank filters (0.5x); (3) the sixth simultaneous breakout (0.5x) and, more importantly, the 52wh exit question P4 in a rolling-over tape; (4) LT Trend at PIT dial 50+ if the gate holds (its solo legs go negative at 65+, its cluster adds do not); (5) the day the projected requirement passes 70% of live NLV, pro rata on new entries, and any day IBKR raises house margin (2020: +35%), where the answer is the futures-routed index legs and the guard, not ATR cuts; (6) pre-print no-stop holders, per name, as today. The step: GRM 1.875 now with the package; 2.25 when the guard, the index-futures routing and the IBKR what-if exist; the per-strategy cap fixed at 250 (OVS 375) through both. Base stays flat $750k until NLV clears it, then half-compounding quarterly. Haircut 40% central with per-strategy keeps, pilots at half their mean, overflow longs at 0.85 until the point-in-time universe lands; commissions and MOC spreads into the engine so the ledger stops being 6% optimistic; the live-vs-ledger reconciliation built from broker fills before anyone re-derives any of this. Seasonality: nothing keys on the calendar; the calendar shows up in this book only as flow, and flow is already the sizing state.
